Study_Title: Quantum-Secure-By-Construction (QSC): A Paradigm Shift For Post-Quantum Agentic Intelligence
Threat_Attacker_Model: Adversaries equipped with fault-tolerant quantum computers (Shor/Grover algorithms) executing Harvest-Now-Decrypt-Later (HNDL) interception, payload tampering, and nonce-replay attacks across untrusted MCP brokers and shared inter-agent memory.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Quantum-Secure-By-Construction (QSC) adaptive 3-layer stack combining NIST PQC (Kyber512/Kyber768 KEM and Dilithium3 digital signatures), hardware Quantum Random Number Generation (ID Quantique Quantis USB 4M QRNG, 4 Mbps), and modeled BB84 Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) with AES-256-GCM.
Enforcement_Point_Location: Sidecar-based QSC Orchestration Gateway mediating 7 critical channels across User, Orchestrator, Agent Workers, MCP Broker, and Shared Memory.
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Post-quantum confidentiality, cryptographic authenticity, and high-entropy replay freshness across session bootstrap, MCP task publishing/fetching, and inter-agent memory sharing (100% block rate on 50,000 tamper and 50,000 replay vectors).
Trust_Assumptions: Underlying lattice assumptions (MLWE/MSIS for Kyber and Dilithium) hold; local sidecar and hardware QRNG USB source are within the trusted computing base; physical QKD fiber links are simulated when unavailable.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Local testbed (Apple M3 Pro): QRNG nonce generation 1.157 ms (~28 Mbps), modeled QKD key establishment 10.0 ms (AES 0.005 ms), channel overheads 0.41 ms (Orch<->Agent handshake) to 9.83 ms (Orch<-MCP aggregation). In Azure PQC-TLS 1.3 deployment, mean channel latency is 297.41–326.00 ms where cloud network RTT (~297 ms) masks cryptographic overhead (Tables 2–5, pp. 14–15).
Exposed_Security_Function: Policy-driven runtime selection and composition of PQC KEM/signatures, QRNG nonces, and QKD-derived session keys across MCP and inter-agent channels.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: QKD Layer 3 links are mathematically modeled rather than executed over physical quantum fiber in Azure cloud zones; sequential signature verification at Orchestrator<-MCP aggregation (Channel 7) creates a 9.83 ms (16,722.9%) local micro-benchmark bottleneck.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: Section 4 & Appendix C (Tables 2–5, Table C.3, pp. 14–15, 40–41): "The PQC implementation uses NIST-standardized key encapsulation and signature schemes... As detailed in Table C.3, the system achieved a 100% rejection rate [across 100,000 injected tampering and replay vectors]."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: Quantum-Secure-By-Construction (QSC) integrates Kyber KEM, Dilithium3 signatures, hardware QRNG nonces, and modeled QKD across seven agent-orchestrator-MCP channels, blocking 100% of 100,000 tamper and replay vectors while adding 0.41–9.83 ms local cryptographic overhead.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Empirical micro-benchmark on Apple M3 Pro with ID Quantique Quantis USB 4M QRNG hardware and Azure cloud-scale PQC-TLS 1.3 integration (N=1..50 workers).
Protected_Object: Inter-agent session keys, Dilithium3 agent identity certificates, MCP task/result payloads, and shared agent memory records.
Composition_Evidence: Composes PQC (Layer 1), hardware QRNG (Layer 2), and QKD/AES-256-GCM (Layer 3) across all 7 channels linking User (B1), Orchestrator/Agent delegation (B2), MCP tool broker (B3), and shared memory/audit (B4).
Coding_Rationale: Ekstraksi teks lengkap PDF (41 hlm.) memverifikasi tolok ukur PQC beban kerja agen (STAGE_5_AGENT_WORKLOAD_BENCHMARK) pada 7 kanal komunikasi lintas B1–B4 (Table 4 hlm. 15, Table C.3 hlm. 41).
Required_Additional_Evidence: Verifikasi independen oleh REVIEWER_1 dan rekonsiliasi lintas-reviewer untuk pengesahan rilis.

Study_Title: Quantum-Secure-By-Construction (QSC): A Paradigm Shift For Post-Quantum Agentic Intelligence
Threat_Attacker_Model: Performance degradation and serialization bottlenecks during concurrent post-quantum cryptographic handshakes and signature verifications in multi-worker agentic MCP deployments.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: PQC-TLS 1.3 (Kyber768 + Dilithium3 + AES-256-GCM) sidecar proxy with parallel worker pool scaling (N=1 to N=50).
Enforcement_Point_Location: Azure Cloud Sidecar Proxy and Orchestrator Aggregation Endpoint (Channels 1–7).
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Linear throughput scaling without serialization bottlenecks across N=1..50 concurrent agent workers under full PQC-TLS 1.3 enforcement.
Trust_Assumptions: Cloud network transport latency dominates raw PQC primitive execution time.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Kyber KEM public key 1,184 B vs 65 B classical (+1,721.5%), ciphertext 1,088 B; Dilithium public key 1,952 B vs 32 B (+6,000%), signature 3,309 B vs 64 B (+5,070.3%), verify 0.08 ms vs 0.03 ms (+149.6%). Azure mean latency is 299.26 ms (Orch->MCP) and 306.83 ms (Orch<-MCP aggregation) vs ~297 ms baseline (Tables 2, 4, 5, pp. 14–15).
Exposed_Security_Function: Quantum-resistant key encapsulation and digital signature verification for MCP tool task publishing and result aggregation.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Sequential signature verification during Channel 7 aggregation adds 9.83 ms local overhead; batch or parallel verification is needed at larger swarm scales.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: Section 4 (Tables 2, 4, 5, pp. 14–15): "The cloud results in Table 5 show a consistent internal latency baseline of approximately 297 ms, indicating that cloud networking dominates total transaction time and largely masks the cryptographic overhead."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: While PQC primitives increase key/signature sizes by 1,721%–6,000% and local aggregation latency by 9.83 ms, Azure cloud deployment latency (297.41–326.00 ms) masks PQC overhead and preserves linear worker scaling up to N=50.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Quantitative RQ3/RQ4 overhead decomposition across raw primitives, 7 local channels, and Azure cloud deployment.
Protected_Object: MCP tool invocation channels and aggregated worker responses.
Composition_Evidence: Quantifies end-to-end latency when composing PQC-TLS 1.3 with QRNG and modeled QKD across multi-worker MCP channels.
Coding_Rationale: Klaim sekunder (-B) diekstraksi untuk menangkap metrik kuantitatif ukuran kunci/tanda tangan PQC dan latensi Azure (RQ3) secara terpisah dari klaim arsitektur utama.
Required_Additional_Evidence: Verifikasi independen oleh REVIEWER_1 dan rekonsiliasi lintas-reviewer untuk pengesahan rilis.

Study_Title: Agentic Witnessing: Pragmatic and Scalable TEE-Enabled Privacy-Preserving Auditing
Threat_Attacker_Model: Untrusted or strategic Prover attempting to misrepresent proprietary codebase/dataset properties or inject prompt-jailbreak payloads in data, and curious Verifier attempting to exfiltrate confidential intellectual property during auditing.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: TEE Remote Attestation (Intel SGX / AMD SEV-SNP / NVIDIA H100 CC quotes binding MRENCLAVE measurement M_AAud), ephemeral Ed25519 key pair (PK_AAud, SK_AAud) generated inside TEE at boot, and SHA-256 hash-chained signed audit transcript verified via TLA+ and Tamarin Prover.
Enforcement_Point_Location: Isolated Auditor Agent container (AAud) executing inside a Confidential Computing TEE and inspecting Prover data via read-only Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools.
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Attested reasoning and privacy-preserving audit integrity: the Verifier receives only Boolean (Yes/No) verdicts bound by an Ed25519-signed SHA-256 hash chain to the dataset hash and TEE hardware quote, with state machine liveness verified in TLA+ and protocol security verified in Tamarin.
Trust_Assumptions: TEE hardware and remote attestation service are trusted; side-channel attacks (cache timing, power analysis, speculative execution) and LLM prompt injection inside audited datasets remain residual risks.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Evaluated on self-audit and 21 systems conference GitHub repositories (SOSP/OSDI/NSDI/ATC, Tables 2–5, pp. 6–8): audits issue 9–91 queries and 45–1,046 MCP tool calls, taking ~20 to 85 minutes (2,009–5,100 s), where LLM inference accounts for 93.4%–98.9% of total runtime and SHA-256/Ed25519 cryptographic signing overhead is negligible.
Exposed_Security_Function: Hardware-attested MCP dataset inspection, SHA-256 transcript chaining, and Ed25519 verdict signing.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Hardware TEE was emulated in the benchmark because the test CPU lacked AMD SEV; Mode B (remote frontier LLM inference) exposes intermediate embeddings/queries outside the CPU TEE unless paired with confidential GPUs (H100); vulnerable to indirect prompt injection embedded in audited repositories.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: Section 2, Section 4 & Appendix A (pp. 2, 5–8, 11): "PK_AAud: Ephemeral Ed25519 public key generated inside the TEE at boot... We modelled the distributed state machine using TLA+ to verify liveness and state consistency, and we verified the cryptographic protocol using the Tamarin Prover."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: Agentic Witnessing isolates an MCP-equipped LLM Auditor inside a TEE with ephemeral Ed25519 keys and a SHA-256 hash chain (verified in TLA+ and Tamarin), auditing 21 GitHub repositories where LLM inference accounts for 93.4%–98.9% of runtime.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Protocol design, TLA+ and Tamarin formal verification, and empirical evaluation across 21 systems repositories using an emulated TEE.
Protected_Object: Proprietary Prover datasets/codebases and Verifier audit transcripts.
Composition_Evidence: Composes TEE remote attestation, MCP tool inspection (B3), and Ed25519-signed SHA-256 audit hash chains (B4) across Verifier, Auditor, and Prover agents.
Coding_Rationale: Teks lengkap PDF (12 hlm.) mengonfirmasi verifikasi protokol menggunakan TLA+ dan Tamarin Prover (TOOL_SUPPORTED_VERIFICATION, hlm. 11) serta ketergantungan pada Ed25519 (STAGE_0_PRE_QUANTUM_ONLY).
Required_Additional_Evidence: Verifikasi independen oleh REVIEWER_1 dan rekonsiliasi lintas-reviewer untuk pengesahan rilis.

Study_Title: MCPShield: A Security Cognition Layer for Adaptive Trust Calibration in Model Context Protocol Agents
Threat_Attacker_Model: Untrusted third-party MCP servers executing tool poisoning, metadata manipulation, indirect prompt injection, and post-invocation behavioral drift across the MCP tool lifecycle.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Non-cryptographic 3-stage adaptive trust calibration layer (MCPShield): Stage 1 Security Cognitive Probing (pre-invocation mock probing & manifest vetting), Stage 2 Isolated Projection (in-invocation parameter/stream inspection), and Stage 3 Periodic Reasoning (post-use behavioral reflection).
Enforcement_Point_Location: Client-side plug-in Security Cognition Layer interposed between the LLM Agent and external MCP servers.
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Lifecycle defense-in-depth calibration of tool trust, raising average defense success rate (1 - ASR) from 10.05% (undefended) to 95.30% across six attack suites and six agentic LLMs while maintaining low false deny rates on benign servers.
Trust_Assumptions: Client-side MCPShield layer and its security cognition prompts cannot be bypassed by external MCP servers.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Across 6 attack suites and 6 LLMs, MCPShield achieves 95.30% average defense rate (vs. 10.05% undefended, Table 1 p. 5; Table 3 p. 8). Conditional triggering in Stage 2 (Tables 4–5 p. 17) and amortized periodic reasoning in Stage 3 (Table 6 p. 18) bound token and runtime overhead to a small fraction of benign interaction cost.
Exposed_Security_Function: Pre-invocation cognitive probing, runtime isolated projection, and post-invocation periodic trust reasoning for MCP tools.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Relies on LLM-based cognitive probing and heuristic manifest inspection without cryptographic tool attestation; adaptive adversaries may craft evasive responses during Stage 1 mock probing.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: Section 1 & Section 4 (Tables 1–6, pp. 2, 5, 7–8, 17–18): "undefended agents are broadly vulnerable, with a 10.05% average defense rate across suites and models, whereas MCPShield reaches 95.30% under the same settings."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: MCPShield couples pre-invocation Security Cognitive Probing, runtime Isolated Projection, and post-use Periodic Reasoning to raise average MCP defense rate (1-ASR) from 10.05% to 95.30% across six agentic LLMs.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Empirical evaluation across 6 MCP attack suites and 6 LLM backbones with stage-wise ablation and overhead decomposition.
Protected_Object: MCP tool selection, invocation parameters, and post-invocation agent reasoning state.
Composition_Evidence: Couples pre-authorization manifest probing (B2), in-invocation parameter projection (B3), and post-execution periodic behavioral reflection (B4).
Coding_Rationale: Teks lengkap PDF (21 hlm.) menunjukkan mekanisme 3 tahap mencakup pra-otorisasi manifest (B2), eksekusi alat (B3), dan refleksi pasca-eksekusi (B4), sehingga dipetakan ke MULTI_BOUNDARY (B2;B3;B4).
Required_Additional_Evidence: Verifikasi independen oleh REVIEWER_1 dan rekonsiliasi lintas-reviewer untuk pengesahan rilis.

Study_Title: MCP-Guard: A Multi-Stage Defense-in-Depth Framework for Securing Model Context Protocol in Agentic AI
Threat_Attacker_Model: Adversarial MCP servers and untrusted external data sources executing indirect prompt injection, tool poisoning, shell/SQL injection, path traversal, and cross-origin data exfiltration.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Three-stage cascaded defense-in-depth pipeline (MCP-Guard) with Neural Backup fallback: Stage I lightweight regex/static detectors (6 detectors including Shell Injection and Cross-Origin Whitelist, <2 ms), Stage II fine-tuned E5 neural embedding detector (~55 ms), and Stage III LLM arbitration for ambiguous interval [Tl=0.45, Tu=0.55].
Enforcement_Point_Location: Inline MCP Security Gateway inspecting tool metadata, invocation arguments, and external server responses.
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Cascaded filtering of syntactic and semantic MCP attacks, achieving 96.01% accuracy (95.1% F1-score) on MCP-AttackBench (70,448 samples) and 89.1% average F1-score (+23.4% improvement) with 51%–13.04x latency reduction compared to standalone LLM guardrails.
Trust_Assumptions: Gateway intercepts all MCP traffic; dynamic cross-origin whitelist is properly configured by the host administrator.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Stage I static filtering <2 ms; Stage II fine-tuned neural detector ~55 ms (96.01% accuracy); full cascaded pipeline averages 455.5–505.9 ms (up to 13.04x speedup vs standalone LLM 6,212 ms; 2.12x–2.77x speedup on 7B models, Tables 4–6, pp. 3–9, 11–14).
Exposed_Security_Function: Multi-stage syntactic regex filtering, fine-tuned neural embedding classification, and selective LLM arbitration with neural fallback.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Average end-to-end pipeline latency of 455.5–505.9 ms when Stage III LLM arbitration is triggered remains too high for ultra-low-latency real-time control or high-frequency trading agents (Section 6, p. 9); non-cryptographic defense.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: Section 3 & Section 5 (Tables 2–6, pp. 2–5, 8–9, 11–14): "Stage I employs optimized regular expressions to intercept overt threats... with negligible latency (<2 ms)... reserving LLM arbitration for edge cases while keeping average latency low (~55 ms)... achieving an average F1-score of 89.1% (+23.4% absolute improvement) and an average latency of 455.5 ms."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: MCP-Guard cascades <2 ms static regex scanners, a ~55 ms fine-tuned neural detector (96.01% accuracy), and selective LLM arbitration with neural backup to reach 89.1%–95.1% F1 on MCP-AttackBench (70,448 samples) with up to 13.04x speedup.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Controlled benchmark across MCP-AttackBench (70,448 samples) and external defense benchmarks across 8 LLM backbones.
Protected_Object: MCP tool schemas/descriptions, tool invocation arguments, and cross-origin server interactions.
Composition_Evidence: Resolves UNMAPPED status: Stage I–III inspect tool metadata/discovery (B2), runtime tool arguments/shell/SQL commands (B3), and cross-origin exfiltration/response auditing (B4, Table 2 p. 4).
Coding_Rationale: Resolusi UNMAPPED: PDF teks lengkap (Table 2 hlm. 4 & Fig. 6 hlm. 11) membuktikan cakupan pada metadata alat (B2), eksekusi argumen alat (B3), dan eksfiltrasi lintas-origin (B4) -> MULTI_BOUNDARY (B2;B3;B4).
Required_Additional_Evidence: Verifikasi independen oleh REVIEWER_1 dan rekonsiliasi lintas-reviewer untuk pengesahan rilis.

Study_Title: API Secrets Should Never Become Tokens in the LLM's Vocabulary: A Threat Analysis of API Credential Handling in LLM Agent Systems and an Empirical Evaluation of a Vault-Mediated Execution Boundary
Threat_Attacker_Model: Prompt injection, tool poisoning, cross-origin redirect attacks, and diagnostic/memory scraping attempting to exfiltrate API keys from LLM context windows, environment variables, filesystem mounts, or trace logs.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Vault-Mediated Execution Boundary (Corvic Security Vault): secrets are stored outside the agent runtime and injected as host-bound HTTP headers only at the outbound proxy boundary for declared target origins (e.g., api.github.com).
Enforcement_Point_Location: External Vault-Mediated Egress Proxy and Host-Bound Credential Injector outside the LLM context and tool execution sandbox.
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Zero raw secret exposure in LLM vocabulary, prompt history, process environment, filesystem mounts, or cross-origin requests across all 16 black-box security probes spanning 7 control domains (16/16 pass rate).
Trust_Assumptions: Vault proxy is non-bypassable for outbound network calls and binds each credential strictly to its declared origin and authentication contract.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Evaluated via 2 controlled black-box experiments (16 probes across 7 control domains on production Corvic Security Vault, Table 2 p. 4): 16/16 (100%) probes met security expectations with 0 secret disclosures; latency overhead not numerically itemized (NR).
Exposed_Security_Function: Out-of-vocabulary credential custody and host-bound egress header injection.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Vault mediation prevents raw key disclosure but does not prevent confused-deputy misuse of authorized capabilities within the allowed origin, nor does centralized custody prevent misconfigured provider authentication contracts (p. 1, Section 9 p. 6).
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: Abstract & Section 6 (Tables 1–3, pp. 1, 3–5): "Across 16 evaluated probes spanning seven control domains, every probe met its expected security outcome... We conclude that vault mediation eliminates several disclosure paths but is necessary rather than sufficient."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: A vault-mediated execution boundary keeps API secrets out of the LLM vocabulary and runtime environment, passing 16/16 black-box security probes across seven control domains without raw credential disclosure.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Threat formalization and two black-box evaluations (16 probes) on a production Corvic Security Vault deployment.
Protected_Object: Third-party API credentials and bearer tokens used by tool-calling LLM agents.
Composition_Evidence: Prevents credential leakage from user/developer prompt ingestion (B1) through agent delegation (B2) to external API execution (B3).
Coding_Rationale: Teks lengkap PDF (7 hlm.) mengevaluasi batas eksekusi termediasi vault produksi (DEPLOYMENT_LIKE_EVALUATION) lintas B1, B2, dan B3 (Tables 1–3, hlm. 3–5).
Required_Additional_Evidence: Verifikasi independen oleh REVIEWER_1 dan rekonsiliasi lintas-reviewer untuk pengesahan rilis.

Study_Title: VIPER-MCP: Detecting and Exploiting Taint-Style Vulnerabilities in Model Context Protocol Servers
Threat_Attacker_Model: Adversary crafting natural-language prompts that steer an LLM agent to invoke vulnerable MCP server tool handlers and pass attacker-controlled arguments into command injection, SQL injection, SSRF, or path traversal sinks.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: VIPER-MCP two-phase vulnerability detection and exploit generation pipeline: Phase I two-pass static taint analysis with containment lookup and vulnerability-anchored call chains; Phase II coverage-guided, penalty-steered (selection penalty rho_chi, chain penalty kappa_chi) dynamic PoC exploit generator.
Enforcement_Point_Location: Static/Dynamic Security Auditing Pipeline over Python/TypeScript MCP server implementations and live LLM agent harnesses.
Security_Property_Guaranteed: End-to-end discovery and dynamic exploit confirmation of taint-style MCP server vulnerabilities, achieving 0% false positive rate (130/130 TP) and 7.7% false negative rate (vs. 24.6%–43.1% FPR and 63.8% FNR for baselines) and discovering 0-day CVEs across real-world MCP servers.
Trust_Assumptions: Auditor has access to MCP server source code (Python/TypeScript covering 83.7% of the MCP ecosystem) and an instrumented execution sandbox.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Evaluated on 130 benchmark cases and real-world MCP repositories (Tables 1–5, pp. 9–13): achieves 0% FPR (130/130) and 7.7% FNR (120/130), outperforming MCPSafetyScanner (43.1% FPR, 63.8% FNR). Per-server analysis runtime averages ~90 seconds (dominated by Phase II LLM exploit generation, p. 12).
Exposed_Security_Function: Two-pass static taint analysis and penalty-steered dynamic PoC exploit synthesis for MCP servers.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Restricted to taint-style vulnerabilities in Python and TypeScript MCP servers (83.7% ecosystem coverage); does not detect business logic flaws, authentication bypasses, or non-taint information disclosure (Section 6, p. 13).
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: Section 1 & Section 5 (Tables 1–5, Table 7, pp. 2, 8–13, 17): "VIPER-MCP achieves a 0% false positive rate (vs. 24.6%–43.1% for baselines) and a false negative rate of only 7.7%... per-server runtime averages ~90 seconds."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: VIPER-MCP combines two-pass static taint analysis with penalty-steered dynamic prompt synthesis to detect and confirm taint-style MCP server vulnerabilities with 0% FPR, 7.7% FNR, and ~90 s per-server runtime, uncovering multiple 0-day CVEs.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Benchmark evaluation (130 cases), ablation across 3 components and 5 LLMs, and real-world 0-day CVE discovery.
Protected_Object: MCP server tool handlers and underlying OS/database/network sinks.
Composition_Evidence: Traces natural-language steering across agent-to-tool invocation (B3) into host OS/network sink execution and forensic exploit confirmation (B4).
Coding_Rationale: Teks lengkap PDF (18 hlm.) memetakan permukaan serangan taint dari pemanggilan alat MCP (B3) hingga eksekusi sink dan audit eksploitasi (B4, Tables 1–7, hlm. 9–17).
Required_Additional_Evidence: Verifikasi independen oleh REVIEWER_1 dan rekonsiliasi lintas-reviewer untuk pengesahan rilis.

Study_Title: VIPER-MCP: Detecting and Exploiting Taint-Style Vulnerabilities in Model Context Protocol Servers
Threat_Attacker_Model: Failure of naive prompt fuzzers to steer LLM agents toward vulnerable MCP tool handlers and satisfy strict parameter schema constraints.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Ablation of VIPER-MCP Anchor Queries, Mutator Scheduling (selection penalty rho_chi, chain penalty kappa_chi), and Feedback-Guided Parameter Penetration across 5 LLM backbones.
Enforcement_Point_Location: VIPER-MCP Phase II Dynamic Exploit Generator.
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Quantifies the necessity of vulnerability-anchored call chains and penalty-guided scheduling: removing Anchor Queries increases FNR from 7.7% to 34.6%, and removing Mutator Scheduling increases FNR to 33.8%.
Trust_Assumptions: Target MCP server is reachable by the test harness.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Ablation study (Table 3 p. 11) shows FNR rises from 7.7% (full VIPER-MCP: 120/130) to 34.6% w/o Anchor Queries (85/130) and 33.8% w/o Mutator Scheduling (86/130); cross-LLM stability (Table 4 p. 13) confirms 83–88 triggered servers across 5 LLMs.
Exposed_Security_Function: Guided multi-intent prompt mutation for dynamic MCP vulnerability verification.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Dynamic confirmation requires live LLM calls (~90 s per server), incurring API cost and latency proportional to call-chain depth.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: Section 5.3 (Tables 3–5, pp. 11–13): "w/o Anchor Queries: 85 TP, 45 FN (34.6% FNR); w/o Mutator Scheduling: 86 TP, 44 FN (33.8% FNR); VIPER-MCP: 120 TP, 10 FN (7.7% FNR)."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: Ablating VIPER-MCP's anchor queries or penalty-steered mutator scheduling degrades dynamic exploit confirmation from 7.7% FNR to 34.6% and 33.8% FNR respectively.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Ablation and cross-model sensitivity benchmark on 130 MCP vulnerability cases.
Protected_Object: MCP tool call routing and type-constrained sink arguments.
Composition_Evidence: Demonstrates how static call-chain anchoring and dynamic prompt scheduling compose to cross the B3 tool-invocation boundary.
Coding_Rationale: Klaim sekunder (-B) diekstraksi untuk mendokumentasikan hasil ablasi kuantitatif dan rincian waktu eksekusi per tahap (Tables 3–5 hlm. 11–13).
Required_Additional_Evidence: Verifikasi independen oleh REVIEWER_1 dan rekonsiliasi lintas-reviewer untuk pengesahan rilis.

Study_Title: SAGA: A Security Architecture for Governing AI Agentic Systems
Threat_Attacker_Model: Dolev-Yao network and malicious-agent adversary capable of intercepting, replaying, reordering, or synthesizing inter-agent messages, exceeding interaction quotas, or initiating unauthorized cross-user agent contact.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: SAGA architecture combining CA-signed X.509/TLS credentials, ECDSA signatures (sigma_UA, sigma_ProvA), Diffie-Hellman One-Time Keys (OTK_A), symmetric AEAD token encryption, quota-bounded access control tokens (Q_max, lifetime L), and Agent Contact Policies (CP_A) formally verified in ProVerif.
Enforcement_Point_Location: Centralized/Sharded SAGA Provider Registry and local SAGA A2A Middleware Stack at each agent.
Security_Property_Guaranteed: ProVerif-verified token secrecy, agent-to-provider authentication, and mutual inter-agent authentication under the Dolev-Yao model, plus user-governed contact policy enforcement and instant agent deactivation.
Trust_Assumptions: Provider is trusted for user registration and policy storage (augmented via sharding/replication in Section V-A); human users authenticate via OIDC; classical ECDSA and DH are computationally secure.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Local cryptographic token derivation/verification overhead t_crypto = 7 ms (p. 11); pre-provisioning OTK batches takes <0.5 s (p. 10); end-to-end task overhead across 3 multi-agent workflows (calendar scheduling, expense report, blog writing) is <0.6% of total execution time (Table II p. 12); Provider sharding scales linearly past 200K reqs/min (Fig. 10–11, pp. 12–13, 19–20).
Exposed_Security_Function: Cryptographic access-control token derivation, OTK-bound A2A handshake, contact policy enforcement, and user-initiated agent deactivation.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Relies on pre-quantum ECDSA and Diffie-Hellman (explicitly motivating the post-quantum MAGIQ successor in ARXIV-S-0057); assumes globally routable public IPs without NAT traversal (Section III-C, p. 5) and trusts the Provider for contact policy evaluation.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: Section IV-F & Section VI (Table II, Figs. 3–5, pp. 9–13): "Using ProVerif's automated reasoning capabilities, we automatically proved each of the aforementioned properties [token secrecy and mutual authentication] with respect to an attacker that can observe, intercept, modify, replay, reorder, and synthesize arbitrary messages... measured cryptographic overhead t_crypto = 7 ms... less than 0.6% of the end-to-end cost."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: SAGA governs multi-agent A2A communication via Provider-mediated contact policies, One-Time Keys, and quota-bounded cryptographic tokens (proved secure in ProVerif), adding 7 ms local cryptographic latency (<0.6% end-to-end task overhead).
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Full open-source implementation (github.com/gsiros/saga), ProVerif formal verification, 8 attacker evaluations, and geo-distributed AWS/CAIDA benchmarks.
Protected_Object: Inter-agent A2A requests, agent registration records, one-time keys (OTKs), and user-defined contact policies.
Composition_Evidence: Binds human user OIDC registration and contact policy specification (B1) to cryptographic OTK-based A2A token derivation and enforcement across multi-agent delegation (B2).
Coding_Rationale: Teks lengkap PDF (23 hlm.) memverifikasi bukti ProVerif (TOOL_SUPPORTED_VERIFICATION, hlm. 9), kode sumber terbuka (PROOF_OF_CONCEPT, hlm. 2), dan ketergantungan pada ECDSA/DH pra-kuantum (STAGE_0_PRE_QUANTUM_ONLY).
Required_Additional_Evidence: Verifikasi independen oleh REVIEWER_1 dan rekonsiliasi lintas-reviewer untuk pengesahan rilis.

Study_Title: SAGA: A Security Architecture for Governing AI Agentic Systems
Threat_Attacker_Model: Latency and throughput bottlenecks from frequent Provider round-trips and short token lifetimes (L) or small request quotas (Q_max) across geo-distributed agent deployments.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Amortized quota-bounded token reuse c_proto(m) = (RTT_B,P + t_crypto) * ceil(m / Q_max) and horizontally sharded Provider registries.
Enforcement_Point_Location: Geo-distributed SAGA Provider shards (US-West, US-East, EU, Asia) and A2A agent endpoints.
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Configurable trade-off between revocation/compromise window (token lifetime L and quota Q_max) and amortized authorization latency, achieving >200,000 reqs/min with linear sharder scaling.
Trust_Assumptions: Provider shards maintain consistent state across partitions.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Deriving 144,000 tokens over 24 hours (L = 1 min) with 100 receiving agents takes <400 s total CPU time (Fig. 3 p. 11). Amortized per-request overhead drops from ~25–220 ms at Q_max = 1 to <10 ms at Q_max >= 20 across US/EU/Asia RTTs (Figs. 4–5 p. 11).
Exposed_Security_Function: Quota-amortized inter-agent token caching and sharded OTK issuance.

Claim_Text_As_Reported: SAGA amortizes Provider RTT and 7 ms cryptographic cost across token quota Q_max (reducing per-request latency below 10 ms for Q_max >= 20) while scaling OTK issuance linearly past 200K reqs/min.

Study_Title: Towards Agentic Cloud Engineering: Graph and Loop Engineering with a Zero-Trust Agent Harness

Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Unified Graph–Loop–Harness Architecture: (1) Graph Engineering with verification-dependent state transitions; (2) Loop Engineering with bounded diagnosis, repair/re-planning, retry (<=20 attempts), and termination; and (3) Zero-Trust Agent Harness enforcing tenant/identity binding, per-action capability authorization, sandboxed execution, and machine-checkable evidence gates.
Enforcement_Point_Location: Zero-Trust Agent Harness & Graph/Loop Execution Supervisor mediating MCP capabilities, execution sandboxes, and Google Cloud APIs (Figs. 6–7, pp. 18–19).
Security_Property_Guaranteed: 100.0% Evidence-Gated Execution Rate (EGER = 420/420), 100.0% Unauthorized Capability Denial Rate (UCDR = 140/140), 99.3% Authorized Capability Permission Rate (ACPR = 139/140), and 100.0% Bounded Termination Rate (BTR = 140/140) across all four evaluated foundation models.

Study_Title: MCPSecBench: A Systematic Security Benchmark and Playground for Testing Model Context Protocols
Threat_Attacker_Model: 17 systematic MCP attack vectors spanning 4 surfaces: Client-Side (prompt injection, command override), Host-Side (tool name squatting, confused AI selection, cross-server shadowing), Protocol-Level (MitM, unauthenticated transport, JSON-RPC tampering), and Server-Side (sandbox escape, RCE, rug pull).
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: MCPSecBench formal MCP execution model F = {f1, f2, f3, f4} and modular evaluation playground testing 3 MCP hosts (Claude Desktop, OpenAI, Cursor) with and without two defense layers: MCIP (secondary judge verification + tool metadata inspection) and FAN (flow/access normalization).
Enforcement_Point_Location: Cross-layer MCP Benchmark Harness evaluating Client, Host, Protocol Transport, and Server execution boundaries.
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Systematic empirical quantification of Attack Success Rate (ASR) and Refusal Rate (RR) across 17 attacks and 3 MCP platforms, demonstrating that over 85% of attacks succeed on at least one platform and existing defenses (MCIP, FAN) fail against protocol/host-level vectors such as package squatting (100% undefended ASR) and MitM.
Trust_Assumptions: Benchmark harness faithfully reproduces MCP client, host, transport, and server interactions.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Across 17 attacks (Table 1 p. 6), average undefended ASR is 48.6% on Claude Desktop (RR 47.6%), 75.2% on OpenAI (RR 10.5%), and 75.2% on Cursor (RR 14.3%). With MCIP, average ASR drops only slightly to 45.7% (Claude), 67.6% (OpenAI), and 73.3% (Cursor); with FAN, average ASR is 78.1% (Claude), 50.5% (OpenAI), and 66.7% (Cursor). Token and USD cost overheads are itemized in Table 4 (pp. 17, 20).
Exposed_Security_Function: Formalized 4-step MCP security taxonomy, 17-attack automated testbed, and LLM-as-a-Judge ASR/RR evaluation.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Evaluated defenses (MCIP and FAN) incur secondary judge token/latency overhead (Table 4 p. 17) yet remain ineffective against protocol-level MitM and host-level tool disambiguation/squatting attacks.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: Section 3 & Section 5 (Tables 1–4, pp. 3–7, 14–17, 20): "F={f1, f2, f3, f4} represents the sequential execution flow... Table 1 summarizes the results across three platforms [Claude Desktop, OpenAI, Cursor] comparing native conditions against two integrated protection mechanisms (MCIP and FAN)."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: MCPSecBench formalizes the 4-stage MCP execution flow and evaluates 17 attacks across Claude Desktop, OpenAI, and Cursor, showing 48.6%–75.2% average undefended ASR and persistent bypasses of MCIP and FAN defenses.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Open-source benchmark and playground evaluating 17 attacks across 4 MCP surfaces and 3 host platforms.
Protected_Object: MCP prompts (f1), tool discovery lists (f2), host tool invocation parameters (f3), and server execution/transport (f4).
Composition_Evidence: Resolves UNMAPPED status: explicitly formalizes f1 user prompt to client (B1), f2 tool list discovery/selection (B2), f3 host-to-server tool call execution (B3), and f4 server execution/return & audit (B4, Section 3 p. 3).
Coding_Rationale: Resolusi UNMAPPED: Model formal F={f1,f2,f3,f4} pada Section 3 (hlm. 3) dan 17 vektor serangan mencakup keempat batas B1, B2, B3, dan B4 -> MULTI_BOUNDARY (B1;B2;B3;B4).

Study_Title: MCPSecBench: A Systematic Security Benchmark and Playground for Testing Model Context Protocols

Exposed_Security_Function: Empirical failure analysis of MCP tool disambiguation and namespace squatting.

Protected_Object: MCP tool namespace resolution and tool selection integrity.

Study_Title: MCP Safety Audit: LLMs with the Model Context Protocol Allow Major Security Exploits
Threat_Attacker_Model: Attacker poisoning external data sources (e.g., vector databases, Slack, GitHub, webpages) to trigger Malicious Code Execution (MCE), Remote Access Control (RAC), and Retrieval-Agent Deception (RADE) across composed MCP servers.

Study_Title: Governance-Aware Agent Telemetry for Closed-Loop Enforcement in Multi-Agent AI Systems
Threat_Attacker_Model: Multi-agent policy violations, unauthorized delegation chains, privilege escalation, and telemetry span forgery or omission across enterprise multi-agent workflows.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Governance-Aware Agent Telemetry (GAAT): (1) Governance Telemetry Schema (GTS) extending OpenTelemetry with ECDSA P-256 span signatures, SHA-256 hashes, AES-256-GCM encryption, and TPM/SGX hardware key anchoring; (2) OPA-compatible streaming policy detector + HMM omission detector; and (3) Governance Enforcement Bus (GEB) with graduated L0–L4 escalation and 4 formal theorems.
Enforcement_Point_Location: Trusted Telemetry Plane and Governance Enforcement Bus (GEB) operating across multi-agent Kubernetes clusters.
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Proves Theorem 1 (Enforcement Monotonicity), Theorem 2 (Escalation Termination), Theorem 3 (Conflict Resolution Determinism under parallel max-action semantics), and Theorem 4 (Bounded False Quarantine), achieving 99.7% Violation Prevention Rate (VPR) and 97.6% violation escape reduction.
Trust_Assumptions: TPM/SGX-anchored ECDSA P-256 keys and Trusted Telemetry Plane are uncompromised; violation arrival rate remains within circuit-breaker bounds.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Across 5,000 synthetic runs and 12,000 empirical production-derived traces (Tables I–IV, pp. 1, 4–5): GAAT achieves 99.7% VPR (0.3% VER, 0.9% FPR with risk-tiered thresholds), 8.4 ms median detection latency, and 127 ms median (192 ms P99) end-to-end enforcement latency (vs. 340 ms for centralized gateway CGW), with 12%–18% resource overhead across 5–20 agents.
Exposed_Security_Function: ECDSA P-256 signed OpenTelemetry governance spans, HMM omission detection, and closed-loop L0–L4 graduated policy enforcement.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Evaluated at 5–20 agent scale (50+ agent enterprise deployment left to future work); relies on pre-quantum ECDSA P-256 signatures; Theorem 4's original independence bound held in 84.38% of runs before correlation correction (Section V-C, pp. 5–6).
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: Section I, Section III & Section V (Theorems 1–4, Tables I–IV, pp. 1, 3–5): "Cryptographic primitives: ECDSA P-256 signatures, SHA-256 hashing, AES-256-GCM encryption... 8.4 ms median detection latency and 127 ms median end-to-end enforcement latency (P99 = 192 ms). On 12,000 empirical production-realistic traces, GAAT achieved 99.7% VPR."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: GAAT binds OpenTelemetry spans with ECDSA P-256 signatures and closes the loop via OPA detection and graduated L0–L4 enforcement (Theorems 1–4), achieving 99.7% Violation Prevention Rate at 8.4 ms P50 detection and 127 ms P50 enforcement latency.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Formal theorems (Theorems 1–4) and benchmark evaluation over 5,000 synthetic flows and 12,000 empirical traces against 4 baselines (Dashboard, GuardAgent, Cedar, CGW).
Protected_Object: Multi-agent telemetry spans, delegation edges, and runtime enforcement state.
Composition_Evidence: Couples inter-agent delegation & tool span instrumentation (B2;B3) with cryptographic audit telemetry and closed-loop quarantine/revocation (B4).
Coding_Rationale: Teks lengkap PDF (6 hlm.) membuktikan 4 teorema (THEORETIC_PROOF), penggunaan ECDSA P-256 (STAGE_0_PRE_QUANTUM_ONLY), dan metrik latensi P50/P99 lengkap pada Tables I–IV (hlm. 4–5).
Required_Additional_Evidence: Verifikasi independen oleh REVIEWER_1 dan rekonsiliasi lintas-reviewer untuk pengesahan rilis.

Study_Title: Who is the 'I' in AI? Establishing Decentralized Identity and Accountability for Autonomous Agents
Threat_Attacker_Model: Sybil agent swarms, silent model-weight swap or behavioral tampering after registration, impersonation across decentralized multi-agent economies, and front-running of revocation transactions.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Four-layer ABCD Decentralized Agent Identity Framework (Algorithmic A_A, Behavioural A_B, Contextual A_C, Decentralised DID/VC A_D) using SHA-256 model weight hashing (modelHash), self-certifying W3C DIDs and Verifiable Credentials, on-chain Verifiable Data Registry (VDR) smart contracts, and mandatory finality challenge window Delta blocks.
Enforcement_Point_Location: On-Chain Verifiable Data Registry (VDR) Smart Contract (C4) and Relying Party Coherence/Authorization Verifier.
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Proves Theorem 1 & Corollary 2 (Behavioural Coherence and Tampering Detection via statistical drift |Phi_Beh - Phi_Alg| > tau), Theorem 3 (Impersonation Resistance under EUF-CMA & DID binding), and Theorem 4 & Corollary 5 (Temporal/Bounded Authorization Enforcement and Front-Running Mitigation when challenge window Delta exceeds finality latency).
Trust_Assumptions: SHA-256 is collision-resistant; underlying signature scheme is EUF-CMA secure; blockchain VDR achieves finality within bounded blocks (<Delta); model swaps induce measurable statistical shifts in monitored behavioural attributes.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Analytical DeFi lifecycle case study (Section VIII, pp. 13–14): monitored 95th-percentile latency baseline 200 ms (sigma = 15 ms, 3-sigma threshold tau = 45 ms) flags tampered model at 280 ms; high-materiality trades (>$10,000) incur a mandatory challenge window of Delta = 64 blocks (~13 minutes vs ~20-block finality latency). No live smart-contract gas or throughput benchmark is executed.
Exposed_Security_Function: ABCD multi-layer DID/VC identity binding, statistical behavioural coherence verification, and finality-gated revocation enforcement.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Behavioural coherence verification (Theorem 1) is probabilistic and vulnerable to false positives from network jitter or false negatives from stealthy tampering within 3-sigma bounds (Section IX, p. 15); evaluated via an analytical DeFi walkthrough without empirical prototype benchmarks.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: Section VII & Section VIII (Theorems 1, 3, 4, Corollaries 2, 5, pp. 11–15): "Theorem 1 (Behavioural Coherence and Tampering Detection)... Theorem 3 (Impersonation Resistance)... Theorem 4 (Temporal and Bounded Authorization Enforcement)... Corollary 5 (Front-Running Mitigation via Challenge Window Delta = 64 blocks)."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: The 4-layer ABCD framework binds static model SHA-256 hashes, runtime behavioural fingerprints, contextual delegations, and W3C DIDs/VCs on-chain, proving Theorems 1, 3, and 4 for tampering detection, impersonation resistance, and front-running-safe revocation.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Formal definitions, four security theorems/corollaries with proofs, and an analytical DeFi trading agent walkthrough.
Protected_Object: Autonomous agent DIDs, Verifiable Credentials, model weight hashes, and high-value delegated DeFi transactions.

Study_Title: CAPMAS: Capability-Based Delegation of Privileges in Multi-Agent Systems
Threat_Attacker_Model: Over-privileged multi-agent delegation chains, confused-deputy privilege escalation across sub-agents, and malicious intermediate agents attempting to remove, reorder, or widen delegated caveats.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: CAPMAS architecture combining (1) Contrastive Learning Semantic Scoping Pipeline (shared encoder + score-drop elbow heuristic alpha=0.2) mapping natural-language user queries to minimal top-k privilege bundles, and (2) Chained HMAC Macaroon tokens supporting offline monotonic privilege intersection and tamper-evident routing caveats.
Enforcement_Point_Location: Central Stateless IAM Provider (root Macaroon issuance & final verification) and Distributed Agent Delegation Middleware (offline HMAC caveat attenuation).
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Monotonic privilege attenuation across multi-hop agent chains (any caveat removal/reordering breaks the HMAC chain) and 99.5% over-privilege reduction compared to full user-identity propagation.
Trust_Assumptions: IAM root secret is confidential; initial semantic scoping at the entry point captures required privileges within the top-k bundle.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Micro-benchmarks (Table 1 p. 10): CAPMAS CreateToken 0.01 ms (0.4 kB), addCaveat 0.01–0.18 ms (0.6–17.4 kB for N=1..100 caveats), Verify 0.01–0.30 ms — 30x faster than Ed25519 Signed Nested (which OOMs >500 MB past depth 15) and 2x lower latency / 3x lower bandwidth than RFC 8693 (Fig. 3 p. 11). On ASTRA & XLAM (3,100+ endpoints, Tables 2–3 pp. 12–13), semantic scoping achieves 92.3% perfect bundle capture (vs 37.4% LLM baseline) with 0.12%–0.47% absolute over-privilege.
Exposed_Security_Function: Contrastive semantic privilege scoping and offline HMAC Macaroon caveat attenuation.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Plaintext caveats in standard Macaroons can be misrepresented to intermediate agents prior to final IAM verification unless state-hash caveats are appended (§9 p. 9); contrastive retriever misses 7.7%–9.1% of ground-truth tool bundles at k=10.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: Section 1 & Section 10 (Tables 1–3, Fig. 3, pp. 1, 10–13): "CAPMAS yields 30 times faster delegation operations, 2 times less delegation-oriented latency and up to 3 times lower network bandwidth overhead, while reducing over-privileging by 99.5%... CreateToken 0.01 ms, addCaveat 0.01–0.18 ms, Verify 0.01–0.30 ms."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: CAPMAS pairs contrastive semantic privilege scoping (92.3% bundle recall, 99.5% over-privilege reduction) with offline HMAC Macaroon attenuation (0.01–0.30 ms verification), achieving 30x faster delegation than Ed25519 nested tokens and 2x lower latency than RFC 8693.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: End-to-end prototype, cryptographic micro-benchmarks (depths 1–100 vs Ed25519 Nested and RFC 8693), and zero-shot retrieval benchmarks on ASTRA and XLAM.
Protected_Object: Delegated API endpoint privileges and multi-hop agent authorization tokens.
Composition_Evidence: Scopes natural-language user intent at B1, attenuates HMAC Macaroons across multi-hop agent delegation at B2, gates tool/endpoint execution at B3, and verifies tamper-evident routing traces at the IAM at B4.
Coding_Rationale: Teks lengkap PDF (20 hlm.) menyajikan perbandingan kuantitatif lengkap antara HMAC Macaroons, Ed25519 Nested, dan RFC 8693 pada Table 1 (hlm. 10) serta evaluasi ASTRA/XLAM pada Tables 2–3 (hlm. 12–13).
Required_Additional_Evidence: Verifikasi independen oleh REVIEWER_1 dan rekonsiliasi lintas-reviewer untuk pengesahan rilis.

Study_Title: Model Context Protocol for Vision Systems: Audit, Security, and Protocol Extensions
Threat_Attacker_Model: Compositional vision toolchain failures, untyped tool connections, privilege escalation via overpermissive tool bindings, silent spatial/coordinate drift, and cross-session memory scoping leaks across vision-centric MCP servers.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Executable MCP Vision Audit Benchmark and Runtime Validators (Schema-format validator, Coordinate-alignment validator, Memory-hygiene validator, and Privilege-verification validator) across 91 public vision MCP servers.

Study_Title: COPEX: Benchmarking LLM Robustness to Adversarial Context Across Model Context Protocol Layers
Threat_Attacker_Model: 25 adversarial context manipulation attack types across 4 MCP entry surfaces (Table 2 & Table 7): Model/Agent surface (prompt injection, goal hijacking), Client surface (config/context manipulation), Server/Tool surface (schema poisoning, parameter poisoning, rug pull), and Transport surface (MCP rebinding, replay).

Study_Title: Agentic Peer-to-Peer Networks: From Content Distribution to Capability and Action Sharing
Threat_Attacker_Model: Open peer-to-peer overlay adversaries launching Sybil attacks, publishing poisoned/inflated or stale capability descriptors (capability drift), or returning fabricated execution results.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Plane-decoupled Agentic P2P Architecture with (1) Cryptographically Signed Soft-State Capability Descriptors CD = <peer_id, sig, endpoints, cap_id, schema_hash, policy_tags, ts, ttl, metadata> and (2) Three-Tier Risk-Adaptive Verification Spectrum (Tier 1 reputation ledger, Tier 2 interactive canary puzzles/microtasks, Tier 3 hardware TEE remote attestation via Intel SGX / ARM TrustZone).
Enforcement_Point_Location: Decentralized/Community Semantic Discovery Registry (PUBLISH/REFRESH/REVOKE) and Requester Tiered Verification Engine.
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Mitigates capability descriptor tampering, stale-capability drift, and adversarial peer execution in open P2P overlays, preventing workflow collapse under up to 30% adversarial peer ratios.
Trust_Assumptions: Peer signing keys and Tier 3 TEE hardware enclaves (SGX/TrustZone) are uncompromised; soft-state TTL refresh intervals bound unannounced capability drift.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Evaluated via discrete-event simulator (github.com/plan-lab-szu/agentic_p2p_sim, N=20..200 peers, attacker ratio alpha=0..0.4, TTL=15s, Fig. 4 p. 6): maintains high task success rate (~0.80–0.90 vs collapse <0.25 without verification) and near-constant median discovery/control-plane latency (~60–100 ms) as network size scales to N=200.
Exposed_Security_Function: Signed TTL-bounded capability descriptor publication/discovery and 3-tier risk-adaptive peer verification.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Evaluated only in an architecture-level discrete-event simulator (excluding packet-level NAT traversal, mobile battery drain, and real LLM/TEE enclave execution latencies, Section VI p. 6).
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: Section IV–VI & Table I (pp. 1, 4–6): "A compact formalization is CD := <peer_id, sig, endpoints, cap_id, schema_hash, policy_tags, ts, ttl, metadata>... verification uses three policy-driven tiers negotiated in the task contract: Reputation (Tier 1), Interactive Challenge-Response canary microtasks (Tier 2), and TEE Remote Attestation (Tier 3)."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: Agentic P2P Networks combine signed, TTL-bounded Capability Descriptors with a 3-tier verification spectrum (reputation, canary microtasks, and TEE attestation), sustaining ~80%–90% task success under poisoning and drift in a 200-peer simulator.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Reference architecture (accepted in IEEE Communications Magazine) and proxy-level discrete-event simulation (N=20..200 peers).
Protected_Object: Peer capability descriptors (CDs), semantic routing tables, and delegated P2P task results.

Study_Title: Sovereign Assurance Boundary: Certificate-Bound Admission for Agentic Infrastructure
Threat_Attacker_Model: Untrusted foundation models proposing destructive or out-of-policy production mutations, stale/manipulated telemetry evidence, replayed or revoked admission certificates, and correlated validator failures.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Sovereign Assurance Boundary (SAB): compiles agent proposals at an Assurance Airlock into typed execution contracts C, binds them to SHA-256 evidence digests H(E), policy version P_ver, and revocation epoch rho_rev, routes by consequence level L(C) (PolicyOnly OPA/Rego, Semantic Quorum Architecture SQA, or Human Multi-Sig), issues Ed25519 admission certificates Omega, and verifies Omega at a Sovereign Broker before execution.
Enforcement_Point_Location: Assurance Airlock, Consequence Router, and Sovereign Execution Broker backed by a PostgreSQL append-only Evidence Ledger.
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Pre-execution certificate-bound admission invariance: no infrastructure mutation executes without a fresh, unrevoked Ed25519 certificate Omega binding contract C, evidence digest H(E), policy version, and broker identity (reducing unsafe admissions to 0.4% while automating 68.2% of human review queue).
Trust_Assumptions: Airlock, Sovereign Broker, Policy/Revocation controller, and Ed25519 signing keys are in the TCB (Table 12 p. 10); external telemetry sources and SQA validators are calibrated.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Go prototype evaluated over 500 execution contracts and 2,500 admission attempts (Table 11 p. 10): PolicyOnly admission latency p50 = 1.84 ms (<5 ms target), Broker Ed25519 + epoch verification latency p50 = 0.15 ms (<1 ms target), Revocation propagation latency p95 = 12.4 ms, SQA quorum latency p50 = 185 ms / p95 = 380 ms, Certificate storage overhead mean = 3.4 KB/action, Routing accuracy = 96.8%, Schema replay completeness = 100%, Unsafe admission rate = 0.4%.
Exposed_Security_Function: Consequence-routed contract compilation, SHA-256 evidence binding, Ed25519 admission certification, and epoch-gated broker verification.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Relies on pre-quantum Ed25519 signatures; consequence classifier R(C) had 3.2% disagreement with expert oracle and 0.4% unsafe admission rate; vulnerable to stale upstream telemetry and human rubber-stamping (Section 9.2 & Table 13, pp. 10–11).

Broker verification latency (p50) 0.15 ms... Revocation propagation latency (p95) 12.4 ms... Unsafe admission rate 0.4%... Certificate storage overhead 3.4 KB / action."

Study_Title: Nautilus Compass: Black-box Persona Drift Detection for Production LLM Agents
Threat_Attacker_Model: Long-session persona and constraint drift in black-box production coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor, GPT-4, Gemini), where agents forget user constraints, repeat flagged mistakes, or confabulate prior agreements.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Nautilus Compass black-box prompt-text hook layer (UserPromptSubmit): combines BGE-m3 bi-encoder cosine similarity over 60 curated behavioral anchors (weighted top-3 mean), time-decayed top-k memory recall, and DPT-style regex/fuzzy strategy injection with an audit-log CLI.
Enforcement_Point_Location: Client-side UserPromptSubmit Hook Daemon interposed before proprietary LLM API calls.
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Black-box detection of behavioral drift (held-out ROC AUC 0.916 vs 0.985 in-set) and long-context memory retrieval (56.6% on LongMemEval-S v0.8 and 44.4% on EverMemBench-Dynamic n=500), significantly reducing confabulation of prior agreements (Delta = +0.42, p < 0.01).

Performance_Overhead_Reported: Warm daemon hot-path latency on CPU-only host (Table 7 p. 13): memory recall ~200 ms, drift scoring (60 anchors) ~164 ms, strategy lookup ~5 ms, total parallel hook latency ~1.8 s (cold start 12–30 s). Cross-encoder reranker adds 36x latency for only +0.0008 AUC gain (Table 2 p. 10).
Exposed_Security_Function: Black-box behavioral drift scoring, episodic memory retrieval, and prompt-hook constraint re-injection.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Provides soft prompt-level steering rather than hard deterministic enforcement; cross-vendor behavior-steering A/B across 6 production LLMs is mixed and axis-specific (Section 1 & Section 6, pp. 3, 15); non-cryptographic.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: Section 1, Section 4 & Section 5 (Tables 1–9, pp. 1–2, 10, 13, 15–16): "Nautilus Compass scores 56.6% on LongMemEval-S v0.8 and 44.4% on EverMemBench-Dynamic (n=500)... warm hot-path latency through the daemon path is ~1.8s (Recall ~200ms, Drift scoring ~164ms, Strategy lookup ~5ms)."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: Nautilus Compass detects black-box persona/constraint drift via BGE-m3 anchor similarity (0.916 held-out AUC) and recalls session memory (44.4% EverMemBench-Dynamic, 56.6% LongMemEval-S) within ~164–200 ms per component (~1.8 s warm hook path).
Assessed_Claim_Scope: MIT-licensed open-source tool (github.com/chunxiaoxx/nautilus-compass) evaluated on LongMemEval-S (500), EverMemBench-Dynamic (500), held-out drift prompts, and 6-vendor LLM A/B steering.
Protected_Object: User-specified coding constraints, behavioral anchors, and multi-session agent memory.

Study_Title: AITH: A Post-Quantum Continuous Delegation Protocol for Human-AI Trust Establishment
Threat_Attacker_Model: Quantum-capable Dolev-Yao network adversary and autonomous AI agent attempting to forge delegation credentials, exceed multi-dimensional operational boundaries, replay revoked authority, or tamper with audit logs.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: AITH (AI Trust Handshake) Post-Quantum Continuous Delegation Protocol: (1) Continuous Delegation Certificate signed once with NIST FIPS 204 ML-DSA-87 (Level 5, 4,627 B signature) binding human principal PK_H and agent model weight hash h_A = SHA-256(model_weights); (2) 6-check deterministic Boundary Engine; (3) sub-second push-based Revocation Protocol; and (4) 3-tier SHA-256 Responsibility Chain.

Study_Title: From Training to Escalation: Forensic Analysis and Local Recreation of RL/RLHF-Induced Privilege Escalation in AI Agents (CVE-2026-65616)

Study_Title: Structural Enforcement of Goal Integrity in AI Agents via Separation-of-Powers Architecture
Threat_Attacker_Model: Agentic misalignment where an untrusted Policy LLM internally constructs harmful sub-goals, attempts unauthorized privilege escalation, or drifts semantically from the user's originating Natural Language Request (NLR).
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Policy–Execution–Authorization (PEA) Separation-of-Powers Architecture: (C1) Typed Policy IR; (C2) Intent Lineage Tracking (ILT) anchoring every intent to nlr_hash = SHA-256(sanitised_NLR || session_id || timestamp); (C3) Goal Drift Detection; (C4) Single-use, state-bound HMAC-SHA256 capability tokens with MinimalCapSet attenuation; and (C5) Output Semantic Gate (OSG).
Enforcement_Point_Location: Deterministic Authorization Rule Engine and Execution Dispatch Gate separating the untrusted Policy LLM from external tool execution.
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Proves six security theorems (T1 Non-Bypassability, T2 No Escalation, T3 Replay & State-Drift Resistance, T4 Audit Completeness, T5 Revocation Soundness, T6 Goal-Integrity Guarantee; Section 4 pp. 8–9), achieving 0.00% enforcement bypass rate across 10,000 trials and 90.5% relative ASR reduction.
Trust_Assumptions: Assumptions A1–A12 hold: HMAC-SHA256 and SHA-256 are secure, signing keys are isolated from the Policy LLM, no alternative dispatch path exists, and human-maintained MinimalCapSet is well-specified.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Evaluated across 3 datasets and 10,000 enforcement trials (Section 5, Tables 1–4, pp. 10–15): 0.00% bypass rate (10,000/10,000 token enforcement), overall ASR reduced to 3.9% (90.5% relative reduction; ablating ILT raises ASR to 21.3%, +17.4 pp), OSG achieves 91.3% precision and 88.2% recall (84.7% vs 21.1% keyword baseline on hardest class). Total P95 runtime overhead is 100–185 ms (Table 4 p. 15).
Exposed_Security_Function: SHA-256 intent lineage anchoring, single-use state-bound HMAC-SHA256 capability tokens, and Output Semantic Gating.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Theorem T6 guarantees lineage traceability and capability containment rather than semantic goal correctness (6.3% false negative rate in semantic drift detection, p. 11 & Section 6.3 p. 13); relies on manual MinimalCapSet configuration (assumption A9).
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: Section 1, Section 4 & Section 5 (Theorems T1–T6, Tables 1–4, pp. 1–2, 8–15): "We prove six security theorems (T1–T6)... Bypass Rate 0.00% (Zero unauthorized executions across 10,000 trials)... Full PEA ASR 3.9% (ASR Relative Reduction 90.5%)... Total estimated PEA overhead is 100–185 ms at P95."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: The PEA separation-of-powers architecture anchors intents via SHA-256 (ILT) and enforces single-use HMAC-SHA256 capability tokens (proving Theorems T1–T6), achieving 0.00% bypass over 10,000 trials and 90.5% ASR reduction (3.9% residual ASR) at 100–185 ms P95 overhead.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Six formal security theorems (T1–T6) with proofs and empirical evaluation across 10,000 trials, ablation studies, and overhead profiling.
Protected_Object: Originating user Natural Language Requests (NLRs), Policy IR intents, HMAC-SHA256 capability tokens, and execution audit logs.

Study_Title: AdapTools: Adaptive Tool-based Indirect Prompt Injection Attacks on Agentic LLMs
Threat_Attacker_Model: Adaptive Indirect Prompt Injection (IPI) attacker embedding stealthy multi-step payloads inside external tool/MCP data responses to hijack reasoning and non-reasoning LLM agents into invoking attacker-chosen tools.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: AdapTools adaptive IPI attack framework: (1) Markov transition probability matrix modeling multi-turn tool-invocation trajectories to select stealthy attack tools with high semantic affinity to benign tasks, and (2) decision-tree-pruned compact strategy library generating adaptive context-aware injection prompts.
Enforcement_Point_Location: External Tool / MCP Data Response Channel targeting the LLM Agent Planner and Tool Selector.

Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Offline construction of the strategy library and tool-transition matrix requires query access to shadow models; does not propose a cryptographic or architectural defense beyond showing the failure of prompt-level guardrails.

Study_Title: OpenKedge: Governing Agentic Mutation with Execution-Bound Safety and Evidence Chains

Study_Title: Sovereign Agentic Loops: Decoupling AI Reasoning from Execution in Real-World Systems

The measured overhead exhibited a median latency of 12.4 ms... no unsafe intent bypassed the evaluation stage... deterministic replay for all 7,500 successfully executed benign actions."

Study_Title: Behind EvoMap: Characterizing a Self-Evolving Agent-to-Agent Collaboration Network

Study_Title: Who Grants the Agent Power? Defending Against Instruction Injection via Task-Centric Access Control

Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: AgentSentry Task-Centric Access Control Framework: (1) Task Interpreter & Policy Generation Engine (PGE) translating user commands into temporary, task-scoped PolicySets (Agent, Resource, Operation, Context) -> {Allow, Deny} from predefined templates; and (2) default-deny Policy Enforcement Point (PEP) / Policy Decision Point (PDP) with automatic task-completion revocation.
Enforcement_Point_Location: Runtime PEP/PDP Mediation Layer on Android Emulator intercepting all GUI and MCP agent actions.
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Task-scoped least privilege and automatic post-task revocation: blocks unauthorized write/send actions injected via untrusted email content while permitting legitimate verification-code reads.
Trust_Assumptions: User initial command is benign; predefined security templates accurately capture minimal required task permissions; PEP cannot be bypassed by the mobile agent.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Validated via a qualitative 1-scenario Android emulator prototype demo ('Register for App X' with injected email exfiltration payload, Section 4, pp. 2–3); no quantitative latency, throughput, or false-positive benchmarks are reported (NR).

Following a default-deny principle, an action is only permitted if an explicit Allow rule matches... The permissions are automatically revoked upon task completion."

Study_Title: Zero-Trust Runtime Verification for Agentic Payment Protocols: Mitigating Replay and Context-Binding Failures in AP2
Threat_Attacker_Model: Asynchronous retry storms, concurrent inter-agent race conditions, mandate replay attacks, and cross-merchant/cross-task context leakage in mandate-based agentic payment protocols (AP2 / UCP).
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Zero-Trust Runtime Verification (ZTRV) for AP2 mandates: combines cryptographic mandate signature verification, deterministic runtime context-binding hash H_ctx = SHA256(task.id || agent.id || merchant.id || scope), and atomic consume-once nonce locking (SetNX with TTL = Delta_t).
Enforcement_Point_Location: Stateless Payment Mandate Verifier and Atomic Distributed Nonce Registry at the Merchant/Payment Gateway.
Security_Property_Guaranteed: 100% interception of mandate replay, cross-context leakage, and concurrent double-spend races with 0.00% false positive rate, while bounding nonce registry memory by peak concurrency rather than cumulative transaction history.
Trust_Assumptions: Mandate issuer signing keys are authentic; atomic SetNX nonce registry provides linearizable lock acquisition within TTL window Delta_t.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Evaluated up to 10,000 transactions per second (TPS) (Section 5, Tables 1–2, Figs. 3–4, pp. 6–9): achieves 100% attack interception (0.00% FPR, Table 1 p. 6), maintains stable average verification latency of 3.7–3.8 ms at 10,000 TPS (dominated by signature verification, while SHA-256 context hashing and SetNX nonce locking add minimal overhead, Table 2 p. 9), and caps peak nonce registry memory at ~12 MB.
Exposed_Security_Function: SHA-256 execution-context hash binding and atomic consume-once mandate nonce verification.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Relies on classical public-key mandate signatures (STAGE_0_PRE_QUANTUM_ONLY) and centralized/distributed SetNX lock availability; TEE integration for hardware-isolated verifiers is deferred to future work (Section 6, p. 10).
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: Section 4 & Section 5 (Tables 1–2, Fig. 3, pp. 1, 5–9): "H_ctx = SHA256(task.id || agent.id || merchant.id || scope)... The proposed framework mitigates all evaluated attacks [0.00% FPR] while maintaining stable verification latency of approximately 3.7–3.8 ms at throughput levels up to 10,000 transactions per second... registry footprint remains modest (~12 MB at peak)."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: Zero-Trust Runtime Verification (ZTRV) binds AP2 payment mandates to H_ctx = SHA256(task.id || agent.id || merchant.id || scope) and enforces atomic SetNX nonce consumption, blocking 100% of replay and context-leakage attacks at 3.7–3.8 ms latency up to 10,000 TPS.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: High-concurrency benchmark (up to 10,000 TPS), 3-vector adversarial evaluation, component ablation, and memory-window sensitivity analysis.
Protected_Object: AP2 cryptographic payment mandates, task/merchant execution context, and consume-once nonces.
Composition_Evidence: Binds user-issued payment mandates (B1) and inter-agent task/scope delegation (B2) to atomic consume-once payment execution at the merchant gateway (B3).
Coding_Rationale: Teks lengkap PDF (11 hlm.) mendokumentasikan rumus H_ctx (hlm. 5), pencegahan 100% serangan pada Table 1 (hlm. 6), dan dekomposisi latensi 3,7–3,8 ms pada 10.000 TPS di Table 2 (hlm. 9).

Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: LoRo-Mark provably lossless and robust agent watermarking: embeds multi-bit copyright messages via HMAC-SHA256 keyed behavior-sequence verification with repetition factor r=3 without altering normal agent action selection on ordinary requests.
Enforcement_Point_Location: Black-Box Ownership Verifier inspecting displayed agent action/behavior trajectories.
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Proves Theorem 1 (Provable Losslessness: zero utility/distribution shift on untouched ordinary requests, Delta_PR = Delta_RS = Delta_TS = Delta_SR = 0), Proposition 1 (No false negatives), Proposition 2 (Fresh-context unforgeability with FPR <= 2^-min(capacity, mac_bits)), Proposition 3 (Prefix truncation robustness above 34.6% retention), and Proposition 4 (Behavior substitution robustness).
Trust_Assumptions: HMAC-SHA256 acts as a secure PRF; defender retains the secret watermark key and can observe black-box behavior sequences of the repackaged agent.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Evaluated on XLAM-Function-Calling-60K across Qwen3-8B, Ministral-8B, and DeepSeek-V3 judge (Tables 1–2, pp. 7–9): 0.00% utility drop across all 4 metrics (vs -3.03% to -16.90% degradation for baseline watermarking schemes, Table 1 p. 8), empirical FPR = 0/10,000 (0.00%; theoretical 5.0 x 10^-5 at 14-bit capacity), and high TPR under behavior substitution and truncation (retaining recovery once >=34.6% of steps survive, p. 9).
Exposed_Security_Function: HMAC-SHA256 lossless trajectory watermarking and black-box ownership verification.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Requires observing at least ~34.6% of the original behavior trajectory steps to decode the watermark under severe truncation (Section 5, p. 9); addresses IP provenance rather than runtime access control.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: Section 4, Section 5 & Appendix (Theorem 1, Propositions 1–4, Tables 1–2, pp. 6–9, 16–17): "Theorem 1 (Provable Losslessness of LoRo-Mark)... LoRo-Mark uses HMAC-SHA256 as the authentication primitive... yielding FPR = 0/10,000 = 0.00% and Delta_PR = Delta_RS = Delta_TS = Delta_SR = 0."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: LoRo-Mark embeds HMAC-SHA256 watermarks into agent behavior trajectories with provable zero utility loss (Theorem 1, 0.00% drop on XLAM-60K vs 3%–16.9% for baselines), 0/10,000 false positives, and provable robustness to truncation and behavior substitution (Propositions 1–4).

Study_Title: A402: Binding Cryptocurrency Payments to Service Execution for Agentic Commerce
Threat_Attacker_Model: Malicious clients (free-riding, double-spending), malicious service providers (collecting x402 payment without executing service or delivering results), and malicious payment vaults or blockchain observers inferring private agent counterparty relationships.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: A402 Payment Architecture: (1) Atomic Service Channels (ASCs) combining AMD SEV-SNP Confidential VM TEE remote attestation with cryptographic Adaptor Signatures to enforce Exec–Pay–Deliver atomicity; and (2) TEE-backed Privacy-Preserving Liquidity Vault aggregating off-chain channel settlements into batch on-chain transactions on Ethereum (Solidity) and Bitcoin (Taproot P2TR).
Enforcement_Point_Location: AMD SEV-SNP Protected Service Provider TEE (S) and Liquidity Vault TEE (U) with Ethereum/Bitcoin Settlement Contracts.
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Exec–Pay–Deliver Atomicity (Definition 2: payment is finalized if and only if the service is executed inside an attested TEE and the result is delivered) and off-chain counterparty/balance privacy against malicious clients, providers, and vaults.
Trust_Assumptions: AMD SEV-SNP CVM hardware and remote attestation are trusted (side-channel leakage is out of scope, Section 3.2 p. 5); underlying adaptor signature and blockchain consensus schemes are secure.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: C++17 prototype on AMD SEV-SNP CVMs with Ethereum and Bitcoin Taproot (Section 6, Tables 1–2, Figs. 6–9, pp. 11–15): achieves peak throughput of 2,875 RPS (single Vault: 2,063 RPS) and sub-second end-to-end latency (~350–372 ms) — 95x faster than Ethereum (~30 TPS) and 410x faster than Bitcoin (~7 TPS), while Liquidity Vault batching amortizes on-chain Ethereum gas and Bitcoin P2TR fees across channels.
Exposed_Security_Function: TEE-assisted adaptor-signature atomic service-payment exchange and private off-chain liquidity vault batch settlement.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Multi-replica Vault coordination reduces throughput from 2,063 RPS (1 replica) to 780.86 RPS (2 replicas) and 250.49 RPS (10 replicas) due to cross-replica state synchronization (Appendix B, Fig. 8 p. 15); relies on pre-quantum ECDSA/Schnorr adaptor signatures and TEE hardware assumptions.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: Section 1, Section 4 & Section 6 (Tables 1–2, Figs. 6–9, pp. 1–2, 8–15): "A402 employs an atomic exchange protocol based on TEE-assisted adaptor signatures, ensuring that payments are finalized if and only if the requested service is correctly executed and its result is delivered... Our prototype achieves a peak throughput of 2,875 RPS with sub-second latency (~350 ms), exceeding Ethereum by 95x and Bitcoin by 410x."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: A402 binds agent service execution to cryptocurrency payment via AMD SEV-SNP TEE-assisted adaptor signatures and a private Liquidity Vault, achieving Exec–Pay–Deliver atomicity at 2,875 RPS peak throughput and ~350 ms latency.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: C++17 implementation on AMD SEV-SNP CVMs with Ethereum and Bitcoin Taproot settlement benchmarks and multi-replica scaling analysis.
Protected_Object: Agent cryptocurrency payments, off-chain Atomic Service Channel balances, and service execution results.
Composition_Evidence: Couples attested service execution and payment commitment at B3 with off-chain liquidity vault state transitions and batch blockchain settlement at B4.
Coding_Rationale: Teks lengkap PDF (17 hlm.) menyajikan implementasi C++17 di atas AMD SEV-SNP + Ethereum/Bitcoin Taproot dengan throughput puncak 2.875 RPS dan latensi ~350 ms (Tables 1–2, Figs. 6–9 hlm. 12–15).
