Study_Title: Same Name, Different Server: A Security Census of Silent Drift in the Model Context Protocol Ecosystem
Threat_Attacker_Model: Supply-chain 'silent drift' and rug-pull attacks in the public MCP registry where a multi-version server silently adds tools, widens capabilities, or redirects its remote endpoint to a new domain under the same server name without bumping a major version.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Full-census static security scanner (31 detection patterns across 8 threat classes, precision-calibrated against 414 manual labels) and multi-version AST/manifest differencing pipeline across 21,643 registered MCP servers (72,606 version records).
Enforcement_Point_Location: Public MCP Registry and Client-Side Package/Server Resolution Boundary.
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Quantifies precision-corrected prevalence of high-severity vulnerabilities (7.6% corrected vs 11.14% raw across 14,353 scanned servers) and proves that servers exhibiting silent capability/endpoint drift have nearly 3x higher odds of a high-severity vulnerability (OR = 2.96), while GitHub star popularity fails to protect users (rho = 0.010, p = 0.308).
Trust_Assumptions: Clients resolve MCP servers by registry name at install/runtime without cryptographic version/capability pinning.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Census of 21,643 MCP servers, 72,606 version records, 14,353 source repositories, and 8,900 multi-version servers (Tables 1–6, pp. 1–2, 6–11): pooled scanner precision is 0.56 across 414 hand-labeled findings; precision-corrected high-severity prevalence is 7.6% (11.14% observed, led by unauthenticated network exposure 6.8% corrected / 9.57% observed and command injection); 40.6% of multi-version servers silently changed advertised tools and 4.16% (370 servers, 441 events) silently redirected remote endpoints, carrying OR = 2.96 for high-severity findings.
Exposed_Security_Function: Precision-calibrated ecosystem vulnerability census and multi-version silent-drift / endpoint-redirection detection.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Pattern-based static scanner (31 patterns) corrects only for false positives (providing a lower bound on true prevalence) and relies on ground-truth labels from a single human rater (Section 6, p. 12).
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: Abstract & Section 4 (Tables 1–6, pp. 1–2, 6–11): "We harvested the full public MCP registry (21,643 servers, 72,606 version records)... 11.14% observed high-severity prevalence reduces to roughly 7.6%... 40.6% changed the tools they advertise silently, and 4.16% (370 servers) redirected their remote endpoint... Servers with silent drift have 2.96 times the odds of a high-severity finding."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: A census of 21,643 public MCP servers (72,606 versions; 14,353 scanned repos) finds 7.6% precision-corrected high-severity vulnerability prevalence, 40.6% silent capability drift, and 4.16% silent remote-endpoint redirections, with silent drift nearly tripling high-severity risk (OR = 2.96).
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Exhaustive August 2026 snapshot census of the public MCP registry with 414-label precision calibration and multivariate logistic regression.
Protected_Object: MCP registry version manifests, tool definitions, remote server endpoints, and handler source code.
Composition_Evidence: Links registry name resolution and silent tool/endpoint drift (B2) to handler command injection/unauthenticated exposure (B3) and ecosystem version provenance (B4).
Coding_Rationale: Teks lengkap PDF (14 hlm.) menyajikan sensus empiris atas 21.643 server MCP publik dengan koreksi presisi 414 label manual (Tables 1–6 hlm. 4–11).
Required_Additional_Evidence: Verifikasi independen oleh REVIEWER_1 dan rekonsiliasi lintas-reviewer untuk pengesahan rilis.

Study_Title: Invisible Threats from Model Context Protocol: Generating Stealthy Injection Payload via Tree-based Adaptive Search
Threat_Attacker_Model: Black-box attacker manipulating external MCP tool responses to inject stealthy indirect prompt-injection payloads that evade perplexity filtering, instruction/sandwich prevention, and recursive summarization.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: TIP (Tree-based Adaptive Search for Stealthy Injection Payloads): black-box tree search with semantic coherence constraints, defense-aware feedback pruning, and dynamic exploration-budget reallocation.
Enforcement_Point_Location: Untrusted MCP Tool Response Channel returning external data into the LLM Agent's unified context window.
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Demonstrates that adaptive tree-based payload optimization achieves >95% Attack Success Rate (up to 100% on 3 of 4 tools) without defenses and sustains >50% ASR (up to 92.0%–97.8% on ExpediaBooking) against rigorous prompt/summarization defenses across four mainstream LLMs.
Trust_Assumptions: Attacker has black-box query access to observe whether candidate tool-response payloads trigger agent actions or defense refusals.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Evaluated across 4 mainstream LLMs (including Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct, GPT-4o, Claude, Llama-3) and 4 tool scenarios (Fraud, Data Steal, Product, Weather/ExpediaBooking; Tables I–III, pp. 7–9): TIP achieves >95% ASR without defense (100% on 3/4 tools) and >50% ASR across all active defenses (e.g., 92.0%–97.8% under Instruction/Sandwich Prevention vs 0%–27.1% for Fixed/GCG baselines), requiring ~480–2,580 search queries per optimization.
Exposed_Security_Function: Tree-based black-box adaptive payload optimization for MCP tool-response prompt injection.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Iterative tree search requires hundreds of black-box queries (~480–2,580 queries, Table I p. 8), introducing optimization latency that limits real-time one-shot exploitation (Section VII-B, p. 12).
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: Section I & Section V (Tables I–III, pp. 1–2, 7–9, 12): "In settings without active defenses, TIP achieves an attack success rate (ASR) exceeding 95% [100% on three out of four tools]... under rigorous defense mechanisms, including perplexity filtering and recursive summarization, TIP sustains an ASR above 50% [up to 97.8%]."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: TIP uses tree-based adaptive search over MCP tool responses to achieve >95% undefended ASR (100% on 3/4 tools) and >50%–97.8% ASR against perplexity filtering, instruction prevention, and recursive summarization across four mainstream LLMs.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Multi-model attack evaluation, cross-model transferability (Table II), and component ablation (Table III) across 4 MCP tool scenarios.
Protected_Object: MCP tool response streams and downstream privileged agent tool invocations.
Composition_Evidence: Injects adaptive payloads into MCP tool responses at B3 to corrupt agent planning and trigger unauthorized secondary tool calls at B2/B3.
Coding_Rationale: Teks lengkap PDF (14 hlm. IEEE TDSC) mendokumentasikan evaluasi serangan TIP lintas 4 LLM dan 4 pertahanan pada Tables I–III (hlm. 8–9).
Required_Additional_Evidence: Verifikasi independen oleh REVIEWER_1 dan rekonsiliasi lintas-reviewer untuk pengesahan rilis.

Study_Title: AIP: Agent Identity Protocol for Verifiable Delegation Across MCP and A2A
Threat_Attacker_Model: Unauthenticated MCP servers (found across ~2,000 scanned servers), scope widening by delegated sub-agents, token replay, cross-domain confused-deputy attacks, and forged completion provenance across MCP and A2A.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Agent Identity Protocol (AIP) with Invocation-Bound Capability Tokens (IBCTs): combines self-certifying/web Ed25519 identities (aip:key:ed25519 / aip:web with RFC 8785 JCS signatures), Biscuit-based Ed25519-signed append-only attenuation blocks, Datalog policy evaluation (recursion-free), transport bindings for MCP (X-AIP-Token) and A2A (aip_identity), and SHA-256 completion provenance blocks.
Enforcement_Point_Location: Local Stateless AIP Middleware (aip-core, aip-token, aip-mcp in Rust and Python) at MCP Servers and A2A Agent Endpoints.
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Public-key verifiable multi-hop delegation, cryptographic scope attenuation (delegatees cannot widen scope without breaking the Ed25519 chain), and 100% rejection across 600 adversarial attack attempts (6 attack classes x 100 iterations).
Trust_Assumptions: Root human/organization Ed25519 private key is uncompromised; verifiers execute the conformance-tested Datalog policy evaluator.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Dual Rust and Python implementations benchmarked on Apple M3 Max (Section 5, Tables 3–8, pp. 11–14): Compact mode verification takes 0.049 ms (Rust) and 0.189 ms (Python); Chained mode scales linearly at 340–380 B/block, taking 0.481 ms at depth 1 and 0.745 ms (Rust) at depth 5; real HTTP MCP call adds 0.22 ms overhead; real multi-agent deployment with Gemini 2.5 Flash adds 2.35 ms (0.086% of 2,749 ms total latency); 100% rejection across 600 adversarial attacks (Table 8 p. 13).
Exposed_Security_Function: Ed25519 identity resolution, Biscuit/Datalog chained capability attenuation, MCP/A2A header binding, and SHA-256 completion provenance.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: AIP v1 uses Ed25519 exclusively, which the author explicitly notes creates a post-quantum migration burden against quantum-capable adversaries (Section 7, p. 16); does not prevent a malicious delegatee from misusing authority within its legitimately granted scope (p. 14).
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: Abstract, Section 5 & Section 7 (Tables 3–8, pp. 1–2, 11–16): "Compact mode verification takes 0.049 ms (Rust) and 0.189 ms (Python)... Reaching 0.745 ms (Rust) at depth 5. In a real MCP deployment over HTTP, AIP adds 0.22 ms overhead... In a real multi-agent deployment with Gemini 2.5 Flash, AIP adds 2.35 ms of overhead (0.086% of total latency). Adversarial evaluation across 600 attack attempts shows 100% rejection... AIP v1 uses Ed25519 exclusively... creates a migration burden if quantum-capable adversaries become a practical concern (p. 16)."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: AIP fuses Ed25519 identities, Biscuit/Datalog chained capability attenuation, and SHA-256 completion blocks into Invocation-Bound Capability Tokens (IBCTs) across MCP and A2A, achieving 0.049 ms Rust verification, 0.22 ms HTTP MCP overhead, 2.35 ms (0.086%) multi-agent overhead, and 100% rejection over 600 attacks.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Dual Rust/Python reference implementation (2,041 LOC, 66 tests), microbenchmarks (depths 0–5), live HTTP MCP & Gemini 2.5 Flash multi-agent benchmarks, and 600-trial adversarial suite.
Protected_Object: Agent identity documents, Invocation-Bound Capability Tokens (IBCTs), MCP/A2A transport headers, and completion provenance records.
Composition_Evidence: Chains human root Ed25519 authorization (B1) through multi-hop A2A delegation attenuation (B2) and MCP HTTP tool invocation (B3) to signed SHA-256 completion provenance blocks (B4).
Coding_Rationale: Teks lengkap PDF (17 hlm.) menyajikan implementasi ganda Rust/Python (Table 3 hlm. 11), metrik latensi sub-milidetik (Tables 4–7 hlm. 11–13), evaluasi 600 serangan (Table 8 hlm. 13), dan diskusi beban migrasi kuantum Ed25519 (STAGE_1_SUGGESTED_MIGRATION, hlm. 16).
Required_Additional_Evidence: Verifikasi independen oleh REVIEWER_1 dan rekonsiliasi lintas-reviewer untuk pengesahan rilis.

Study_Title: AIP: Agent Identity Protocol for Verifiable Delegation Across MCP and A2A
Threat_Attacker_Model: Six adversarial delegation attack classes: scope widening, expired token replay, cross-domain confused deputy, signature tampering, delegation depth violation, and completion provenance forgery.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Comparative adversarial evaluation of AIP Chained IBCTs (Ed25519 + Datalog + SHA-256 completion block) vs. Unsigned/Static JWTs across 600 attack trials.
Enforcement_Point_Location: AIP Token Verifier and Datalog Policy Engine.
Security_Property_Guaranteed: 100% rejection rate (600/600) across all six attack classes, whereas static JWT baselines fail against scope widening, delegation depth violations, and completion forgery.
Trust_Assumptions: Verifier checks all Ed25519 block signatures and Datalog attenuation facts locally.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Across 600 adversarial trials (100 per attack class, Table 8 p. 13), AIP achieves 100% rejection across all 6 classes with linear token size growth of 340–380 bytes per delegation block and 0.481–0.745 ms Rust verification latency across depths 1–5 (Table 5 p. 12).
Exposed_Security_Function: Adversarial rejection and linear depth scaling of Ed25519-chained Biscuit/Datalog tokens.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Local localhost HTTP benchmarks do not capture WAN cross-domain key-resolution caching latencies or revocation list distribution (Section 7, p. 15).
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: Section 5.2 & Section 5.5 (Tables 5 & 8, pp. 12–14): "linear scaling of chained tokens at 340–380 bytes per delegation block... Verification latency grows linearly, reaching 0.745 ms (Rust) at depth 5... Adversarial security evaluation (100 iterations per attack, 600 total): 100% rejection."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: AIP's chained IBCT tokens scale linearly at 340–380 bytes/block (0.745 ms Rust verification at depth 5) and reject 100% of 600 adversarial delegation and provenance attacks.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Depth-scaling microbenchmark (depths 0–5) and 600-iteration adversarial test suite.
Protected_Object: Chained delegation blocks and completion provenance hashes.
Composition_Evidence: Quantifies multi-hop delegation scaling (B2), MCP tool verification (B3), and completion block integrity (B4).
Coding_Rationale: Klaim sekunder (-B) diekstraksi untuk mendokumentasikan penskalaan kedalaman delegasi 0–5 (Table 5 hlm. 12) dan evaluasi 600 serangan (Table 8 hlm. 13) pada RQ3.
Required_Additional_Evidence: Verifikasi independen oleh REVIEWER_1 dan rekonsiliasi lintas-reviewer untuk pengesahan rilis.

Study_Title: WAAA! Web Adversaries Against Agentic Browsers
Threat_Attacker_Model: Web adversaries targeting agentic browsers (See->Act LLM browsers such as ChatGPT Operator, Perplexity Comet, Claude Computer Use, BrowserOS) using 20 traditional and novel web social-engineering, UI mimicry, same-site action confusion (SS-4), and domain/path slop-squatting (SQ-1, SQ-2) attacks without relying on explicit prompt injection.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Systematic 60-combination Threat Model & 20-Attack Taxonomy for Agentic Browsers (10 mapped to traditional web security + 10 novel LLM-browser attacks) evaluated via 18 proof-of-concept web pages across Playwright-integrated LLMs and commercial agentic browsers.
Enforcement_Point_Location: Agentic Browser See->Act Perception and DOM/GUI Action Execution Boundary.
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Demonstrates that prompt-injection filters alone cannot secure agentic browsers because visual/DOM deception, phishing, clickjacking, and LLM slop-squatting induce autonomous agents to execute privileged actions and exfiltrate credentials across commercial and open-source browsers.
Trust_Assumptions: Agentic browser autonomously reads untrusted web DOM/visual state and executes privileged user session actions.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Evaluated across 20 taxonomy attack classes using 18 PoC webpages (14 automated via Playwright across multiple LLMs + commercial browser testing on BrowserOS, Perplexity, etc., Tables 1–4, pp. 6, 10–16): confirms widespread susceptibility across vendors, though December 2025 BrowserOS system-prompt confirmation updates mitigated a subset of attacks by deferring to the user (p. 10).
Exposed_Security_Function: 20-attack web adversary taxonomy and PoC evaluation benchmark for agentic browsers.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Automated Playwright evaluation covers 14 of the 18 PoCs across single-page setups; live commercial browser behavior fluctuates with vendor system-prompt updates and anti-bot proxies (Section 6, pp. 10–11).
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: Section 1, Section 4 & Section 6 (Tables 1–4, pp. 1, 5–6, 9–12, 16): "by failing to consider traditional web attacks, previous agentic browser threat models have a blind spot to web social engineering attacks... we found 20 attacks (described in Table 1), 10 that map to existing web security literature and 10 that do not have a clear analog."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: WAAA! derives a 20-attack taxonomy (10 traditional web attacks + 10 novel agentic attacks such as slop-squatting) from 60 threat combinations and validates 18 PoC webpages against LLM agentic browsers, showing that visual/UI deception bypasses prompt-injection defenses.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: 60-combination threat taxonomy, 11-browser capability survey (Table 4), and 18-PoC empirical evaluation across Playwright LLMs and BrowserOS.
Protected_Object: Agentic browser DOM/visual perception (See), autonomous navigation/planning, and privileged web session actions (Act).
Composition_Evidence: Resolves UNMAPPED status: web adversaries exploit the See->Act loop across user intent/confirmation ambiguity (B1), URL/domain discovery & slop-squatting routing (B2), and privileged browser DOM/HTTP action execution (B3, Section 2.2 & Table 1, pp. 3–6).
Coding_Rationale: Resolusi UNMAPPED: PDF teks lengkap (17 hlm.) memodelkan siklus See->Act pada peramban agen lintas ambiguitas intensi pengguna (B1), penemuan domain/slop-squatting (B2), dan eksekusi aksi web berprivilese (B3) -> MULTI_BOUNDARY (B1;B2;B3).
Required_Additional_Evidence: Verifikasi independen oleh REVIEWER_1 dan rekonsiliasi lintas-reviewer untuk pengesahan rilis.

Study_Title: StegoMemory: Agentic Memory Acts as Covert Steganographic Channel
Threat_Attacker_Model: Covert cross-session steganographic attack where an adversary induces an LLM agent in Session 1 to encode secret strings (using Acrostic, Mesostic, Telestich, Word-choice, Capitalization, Position-based, or Homoglyph schemes) into persistent memory so they survive summarization/storage and are recovered in Session 2 without triggering safety oversight.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: StegoMemory 5-stage red-teaming benchmark and deterministic decoder suite evaluating 7 steganographic encoding schemes across 13 frontier/open models, 91 model-attack configurations, and 14,000 SHADE-Arena-style attack trials with independent task-completion and safety oversight.
Enforcement_Point_Location: Agent Persistent Memory Write, Summarization, Retrieval, and Safety Oversight Pipeline.
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Demonstrates that agentic persistent memory acts as a viable covert steganographic channel: across 14,000 trials, 41.2% encode the payload in the response, and 71.4% of exact-match memory recoveries pass both task-completion and independent safety oversight.
Trust_Assumptions: Attacker can plant a side-task instruction in Session 1 and observe or trigger memory retrieval in Session 2.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Evaluated across 14,000 attack trials (100 main-task seeds, 2,000 synthetic credential-like secrets, 13 models x 7 schemes = 91 configs; Tables 1–9, Fig. 9, pp. 1, 7–14, 22–26): 41.2% of trials encode the target payload in Session 1 output; memory persistence/summarization is the primary bottleneck, yet among exact-match cross-session transmissions, 71.4% evade independent safety oversight (p. 24). For 9 of 13 models, malformed encoding rate M_m exceeds refusal rate R_m (p. 9, Table 8 p. 26).
Exposed_Security_Function: Cross-session steganographic memory channel benchmarking and stage-wise funnel bottleneck analysis.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Uses static encoding schemes, synthetic secrets, and offline deterministic decoders across isolated write/retrieval sessions without measuring downstream tool-execution exploitation (Section 6.10, Table 10, pp. 27–28).
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: Abstract, Section 3 & Section 6 (Tables 1–9, pp. 1, 9–14, 22–27): "We test 14,000 attack trials spanning 91 model–attack configurations, 13 models, and 7 steganographic schemes... 41.2% of trials successfully encode the target payload in the generated response... of exact-match transmissions, 71.4% also pass task completion and independent safety oversight."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: Across 14,000 red-teaming trials (13 LLMs, 7 steganographic schemes), StegoMemory shows that 41.2% of trials encode covert payloads into agent outputs and 71.4% of exact-match cross-session memory recoveries evade independent safety oversight.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: 45-page red-teaming benchmark across 14,000 trials, 13 models, 7 steganographic schemes, and a 120-trial human annotation study.
Protected_Object: Cross-session episodic/semantic agent memory stores and safety oversight monitors.
Composition_Evidence: Resolves UNMAPPED status: embeds covert side-tasks during prompt/context ingestion (B1), executes memory write/read tool operations (B3), and persists/retrieves steganographic payloads across long-term memory and oversight auditing (B4, Table 2 p. 14).
Coding_Rationale: Resolusi UNMAPPED: PDF teks lengkap (45 hlm.) memetakan rantai serangan StegoMemory dari injeksi tugas sampingan pada input (B1), operasi penulisan/pengambilan memori (B3), hingga persistensi memori lintas-sesi dan pengawasan audit (B4, Table 2 hlm. 14) -> MULTI_BOUNDARY (B1;B3;B4).
Required_Additional_Evidence: Verifikasi independen oleh REVIEWER_1 dan rekonsiliasi lintas-reviewer untuk pengesahan rilis.

Study_Title: Beyond Attack-Success Rate: Action-Graded Severity Scale for Tool-Using AI Agents
Threat_Attacker_Model: Indirect prompt injection attacks on tool-using workspace agents where binary Attack-Success Rate (ASR) hides partial cross-scope side effects, irreversible external actions, or multi-step privilege escalation chains.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: 7-Level Action-Graded Harm Rubric (L0 benign/no-op to L6 multi-step escalating chain based on reversibility, cross-scope external reach, and privilege expansion) computed by (1) a deterministic programmatic trajectory oracle O and (2) a 3-model tag-free LLM-as-a-Judge panel.
Enforcement_Point_Location: Post-Execution Tool-Call Trajectory Oracle and Audit Evaluator over AgentDojo Workspace traces.
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Exposes three critical failure modes invisible to binary ASR: (1) a tool-filter defense reporting 0% binary ASR while still leaking an L3 cross-scope action; (2) a spotlighting defense that lowers binary ASR from 48% to 40% while tripling worst-case L5+L6 severity tail episodes (from 1 to 3); and (3) high reliability between the programmatic oracle and 3-judge panel (ordinal Krippendorff's alpha = 0.87).
Trust_Assumptions: Evaluator has access to the complete tool-call trajectory and tool-effect metadata table (Table III).
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Evaluated over AgentDojo workspace suite across 4 victim models, 2 defenses (tool filter, spotlighting), and 188 multi-judge episodes (Tables I–V, pp. 3–7): programmatic oracle adds zero model calls and negligible deterministic compute; 3-judge panel achieves ordinal Krippendorff's alpha = 0.87 against the oracle (Table II p. 5).
Exposed_Security_Function: Deterministic and multi-judge action-graded severity scoring (L0–L6) over agent tool-call trajectories.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Programmatic oracle requires a manually curated tool-effect metadata table (10 consequential workspace tools in Table III p. 7) and a distinguishable attacker target (Section VII, pp. 3, 5–6).
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: Section I, Section IV & Section V (Tables I–V, pp. 1–5, 7): "three concrete cases where binary and severity scoring disagree: a defense that reports a 0% ASR while still leaking a cross-scope action; a defense that lowers ASR [48% to 40%] while raising the worst-case severity tail [L5+L6 from 1 to 3 episodes]... ordinal Krippendorff's alpha is 0.87."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: An L0–L6 action-graded severity rubric and deterministic trajectory oracle (Krippendorff's alpha = 0.87 with 3 LLM judges) reveal that defenses reporting 0% or reduced binary ASR on AgentDojo still leak cross-scope actions or triple L5–L6 tail severity.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Evaluation across 4 victim models, 2 defenses, and 188 episodes on the AgentDojo workspace benchmark.
Protected_Object: Workspace tool-call trajectories, cross-scope email/cloud actions, and privilege-expanding tool chains.
Composition_Evidence: Evaluates how prompt-injection defenses at B2 affect consequential tool executions at B3 and trajectory-level harm auditing at B4.
Coding_Rationale: Teks lengkap PDF (8 hlm.) membuktikan secara empiris kegagalan metrik ASR biner melalui rubrik L0–L6 pada AgentDojo (Tables I–V hlm. 3–7).
Required_Additional_Evidence: Verifikasi independen oleh REVIEWER_1 dan rekonsiliasi lintas-reviewer untuk pengesahan rilis.

Study_Title: Byzantine Fault-Tolerant Multi-Agent System for Healthcare: A Gossip Protocol Approach to Secure Medical Message Propagation
Threat_Attacker_Model: Byzantine faulty or compromised medical AI agents (up to f faulty nodes among n = 3f + 1 agents) injecting forged clinical messages, replaying expired emergency alerts, or propagating malformed diagnostic conclusions.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Byzantine Fault-Tolerant Healthcare Multi-Agent Gossip Protocol: combines (1) SHA-256 message digest binding sigma_m = SHA256(id_m || type_m || content_m || t_m || sender_m) with timestamp freshness checks (|t_now - t_m| <= Delta_t), (2) epidemic gossip propagation (fanout k=3), and (3) 2f + 1 supermajority BFT consensus voting across 4 specialized Claude 3.7 Sonnet clinical agents.
Enforcement_Point_Location: Inter-Agent Gossip Validation Layer and BFT Consensus Coordinator across clinical agents (Diagnosis, Treatment Planning, Emergency Response, Data Analysis).
Security_Property_Guaranteed: 100% consensus accuracy across valid clinical messages and 100% rejection of Byzantine injections (invalid signatures, expired timestamps, malformed payloads) when faulty nodes f < n/3 (up to 33% Byzantine nodes).
Trust_Assumptions: Fewer than 1/3 of participating clinical agents are Byzantine (n >= 3f + 1); SHA-256 is collision-resistant; node clocks are synchronized within Delta_t.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Evaluated over 100 clinical messages (4 types x 25), 50 injected Byzantine faults, and 1,000 consensus rounds (Section VI, Tables I–II, Figs. 3–6, pp. 5–6): achieves 100% consensus acceptance (100/100) and 100% Byzantine fault rejection (20/20 invalid signatures, 15/15 expired timestamps, 15/15 malformed content); mean gossip propagation latency is 12.3 +/- 2.1 ms and mean total BFT consensus duration is 45.7 ms (p95 < 100 ms), scaling linearly at ~2.1 ms per added agent up to 31 agents.
Exposed_Security_Function: SHA-256 + timestamp gossip message validation and 2f+1 Byzantine quorum consensus for multi-agent clinical decisions.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Equation (3) on p. 2 defines sigma_m = SHA256(id_m || type_m || content_m || t_m || sender_m) as an unkeyed SHA-256 hash rather than an asymmetric digital signature or keyed HMAC, which would allow any node knowing the public fields to recompute sigma_m unless paired with private signing keys; evaluated on a 4-agent simulated network.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: Section III & Section VI (Eq. 3, Tables I–II, Figs. 5–6, pp. 2, 5–7): "sigma_m = SHA256(id_m || type_m || content_m || t_m || sender_m)... Table I: 100% Consensus Accuracy (100/100)... Table II: 100% rejection of Byzantine messages (50/50)... Average propagation latency was 12.3 +/- 2.1 ms... mean consensus latency of 45.7 ms."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: A Byzantine fault-tolerant healthcare multi-agent system combines gossip propagation, SHA-256 + timestamp message validation, and 2f+1 consensus across four Claude 3.7 Sonnet agents, achieving 100% Byzantine message rejection at 12.3 ms propagation and 45.7 ms mean consensus latency.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: 4-agent healthcare MAS prototype and 1,000-round consensus latency/scalability simulation up to 31 agents.
Protected_Object: Inter-agent clinical messages (Patient Data, Diagnosis, Treatment Plan, Emergency Alert) and consensus decisions.
Composition_Evidence: Resolves UNMAPPED status: secures peer-to-peer inter-agent gossip communication and consensus coordination (B2) while logging and rejecting Byzantine fault injections across the clinical audit trail (B4, Tables I–II p. 5).
Coding_Rationale: Resolusi UNMAPPED & Audit Kritis: Dipetakan ke MULTI_BOUNDARY (B2;B4). Dicatat kelemahan desain kritis pada Persamaan (3) hlm. 2 di mana 'signature' sigma_m dirumuskan hanya sebagai hash SHA-256 tanpa kunci rahasia (DG;AD;UG, PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED).
Required_Additional_Evidence: Verifikasi independen oleh REVIEWER_1 dan rekonsiliasi lintas-reviewer untuk pengesahan rilis.

Study_Title: MemMorph: Tool Hijacking in LLM Agents via Memory Poisoning
Threat_Attacker_Model: Long-term memory poisoning attacker injecting a small budget (n=3) of stealthy records disguised as technical facts, incident reports, or operational policies into an agent's external memory module (e.g., Mem0, MemoryOS) to hijack downstream tool selection without modifying tool metadata.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: MemMorph Memory-Poisoning Tool Hijacking Framework: combines (1) survival-aware anchor markers (12 markers across 4 categories with >80% memory-abstraction retention, Table 6 p. 11) and (2) beam-search shadow-model optimization aligning poisoned seeds with retrieval queries and biasing tool selection toward t_risk over t_safe.
Enforcement_Point_Location: Agent Long-Term Memory Write/Compression Store (Mem0 / MemoryOS) and Memory-Augmented Tool Selection Context.
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Demonstrates that poisoning only 3 memory records achieves 92.3% average Anchor Hit Rate (AHR) and surpasses the strongest baseline by 14.7%–25.9% in Attack Success Rate (ASR) across 3 benchmarks and 10 LLM backbones, sustaining >67% ASR across memory modules and >50% ASR against PPL Filter, Distil Classifier, and Memory Auditor defenses.
Trust_Assumptions: Attacker can inject up to n=3 records into the memory store (via direct or indirect poisoning) and has white-box knowledge of the memory module architecture.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Evaluated across 3 benchmarks, 10 agent backbone LLMs, 3 memory modules (including Mem0 and MemoryOS), and 3 defenses (Tables 1–5, pp. 6–8): MemMorph achieves 92.3% average AHR, outperforms baselines by 14.7%–25.9% ASR under direct and indirect poisoning, retains high ASR despite 6.7x memory growth, incurs only 9.9% storage overhead, and requires <8 ms spaCy parsing overhead per payload (p. 11).
Exposed_Security_Function: Abstraction-surviving memory seed optimization and memory-driven tool hijacking evaluation.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Assumes white-box knowledge of the memory extraction/abstraction prompts (Section 7, p. 9); does not implement a cryptographic memory-provenance defense.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: Section 1, Section 5 & Tables 1–5 (pp. 1–2, 6–8): "MemMorph, the first attack that biases tool selection by poisoning the agent's long-term memory... surpasses the strongest baseline by 14.7–25.9% in average ASR across all three datasets... AHR averaged 92.3%... retains above 67% ASR on both memory modules [Mem0 and MemoryOS]."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: MemMorph poisons agent long-term memory (Mem0, MemoryOS) using abstraction-surviving anchors and beam search, achieving 92.3% retrieval hit rate and +14.7%–25.9% higher tool-hijacking ASR than baselines across 10 LLMs while bypassing three memory defenses.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Evaluation across 3 benchmarks, 10 LLMs, 3 memory systems, component ablations, and 3 defense mechanisms.
Protected_Object: Long-term episodic/semantic agent memory stores (Mem0, MemoryOS) and memory-conditioned tool selection.
Composition_Evidence: Poisons persistent memory records at B4 so that retrieved memories bias tool selection at B2 and trigger high-risk tool invocation at B3.
Coding_Rationale: Teks lengkap PDF (17 hlm.) membuktikan pembajakan pemilihan alat melalui peracunan memori jangka panjang pada 10 LLM dan 3 modul memori (Tables 1–6 hlm. 6–11).
Required_Additional_Evidence: Verifikasi independen oleh REVIEWER_1 dan rekonsiliasi lintas-reviewer untuk pengesahan rilis.

Study_Title: Building Trust in Autonomous Commerce: A Verifiable Global Event Timeline and AI-Ready Fraud Intelligence Layer
Threat_Attacker_Model: Retroactive log tampering, cross-platform timestamp manipulation, repudiation of high-value autonomous agent transactions, and poisoning of fraud-detection AI training labels across siloed commerce platforms (AP2 / ACP).
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Verifiable Global Event Timeline & AI-Ready Fraud Intelligence Layer: (1) domain-separated SHA-256 canonical event hashing E_i = H(Serialize(txID, eventType, participantID, timestamp, payloadHash)); (2) deterministic batch ordering and binary SHA-256 Merkle tree construction; (3) periodic 32-byte Merkle root anchoring on Ethereum/L2; and (4) cryptographically provenance-bound fraud labels for GNN training.
Enforcement_Point_Location: Cross-Domain Event Anchoring Service and Merkle Inclusion Verifier above AP2/ACP commerce platforms.
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Tamper-evident global event ordering and O(log N) inclusion verification across autonomous commerce domains: any modification to a historical event or fraud label invalidates the anchored 32-byte SHA-256 Merkle root.
Trust_Assumptions: SHA-256 is collision-resistant; underlying blockchain (Ethereum/L2) provides immutable finality for anchored roots; at least one honest observer retains off-chain event batch payloads.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Python prototype benchmarked across batch sizes of 1,000 to 50,000 events (Section 12, Tables 1–4, pp. 1, 13–15): Merkle tree construction takes 0.89 ms (1,000 events) to 46.95 ms (50,000 events, <0.1% of a 60 s anchoring period, sustaining ~1,061 events/s); inclusion proof size scales logarithmically from 320 B (1,000 events) to 512 B (50,000 events); end-to-end verification latency is 0.0083–0.0123 ms at 50,000 events (14.4x faster than linear scan 0.1188 ms, Table 4 p. 15).
Exposed_Security_Function: Deterministic cross-domain event batching, SHA-256 Merkle tree anchoring, and sub-millisecond inclusion proof verification.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Does not prevent event omission by a platform prior to batch anchoring ('distributed omission detection' deferred to future work), nor does it guarantee off-chain payload storage availability or veracity of the fraud labeler itself (Section 13, p. 16).
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: Abstract & Section 12 (Tables 1–4, pp. 1, 13–16): "Merkle tree construction scales linearly from 0.89 ms (1,000 events) to 46.95 ms (50,000 events); proof sizes grow logarithmically from 320 bytes at 1,000 events to only 512 bytes at 50,000 events; and Merkle-based verification [0.0083–0.0123 ms] outperforms linear scan by up to 14.4x."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: A verifiable global event timeline hashes AP2/ACP commerce events into domain-separated SHA-256 Merkle trees anchored on-chain, building 50,000-event trees in 46.95 ms with 512-byte proofs that verify in 0.0083–0.0123 ms (14.4x faster than linear scan).
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Protocol specification and empirical Merkle construction/verification benchmarks from 1,000 to 50,000 events.
Protected_Object: Cross-domain autonomous commerce event logs and AI fraud-detection training labels.
Composition_Evidence: Aggregates multi-platform agent transaction logs and fraud labels into a unified tamper-evident SHA-256 Merkle audit substrate at B4.
Coding_Rationale: Teks lengkap PDF (18 hlm.) menyajikan metrik kuantitatif lengkap konstruksi dan verifikasi pohon Merkle SHA-256 pada Tables 1–4 (hlm. 13–15) serta 4 batasan residu pada Section 13 (hlm. 16).
Required_Additional_Evidence: Verifikasi independen oleh REVIEWER_1 dan rekonsiliasi lintas-reviewer untuk pengesahan rilis.

Study_Title: Governed Individuation: Cryptographically Decoupling an Agent's Learning from Its Authority
Threat_Attacker_Model: Deployed self-improving / continual-learning agents under reward pressure or indirect prompt injection that synthesize new skills, induce flawed governance principles in episodic memory, or obfuscate shell/file commands (across 8 indirection encodings) to tamper with evaluation/secret/policy artifacts.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Governed Individuation Architecture: (1) operator-signed authority ceiling S bound to an immutable SHA-256 identity digest H(commitment); (2) non-learning Runtime Reference Monitor & Semantic-Effect Verifier A gating actions by semantic effect against lattice ceiling l_S; and (3) append-only hash-chained audit log.
Enforcement_Point_Location: Non-Learning Runtime Reference Monitor and In-Container Effect Tracer gating all skill compositions and tool executions.
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Proves Theorem 1 (Permission-boundary conservation under learned mediation: executed authority never exceeds l_S up to verifier residual delta_A(n)), Theorem 2 (Containment under open-ended skill composition over a fixed lattice), Theorem 3 (Signature-gated boundary widening requiring operator key), and Theorem 4 (Refusal bound from imperfect induction), reducing executed forbidden writes in ToolGym-GI to zero.
Trust_Assumptions: Fixed non-learning effect monitor A and in-container runtime effect tracer are in the TCB; operator signing key is uncompromised.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Evaluated across 3 open-weight model families (Mistral, Qwen, Phi) on a 14-task governance-decision benchmark, the open-ended ToolGym-GI repository benchmark, and a 320-attempt adversarial verifier-bypass suite (4 effect classes x 8 indirection encodings; Tables 1–2, pp. 8–17): ungoverned agents under reward pressure execute forbidden evaluation/policy writes, whereas Governed Individuation reduces executed forbidden effects to 0% and runtime effect tracing closes the verifier false-allow rate delta_A across all 8 indirection encodings (Table 2 p. 17).
Exposed_Security_Function: Cryptographically committed authority ceiling H(commitment), lattice-based semantic-effect gating over composed skills, and runtime effect tracing.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Containment guarantee is conditional on the soundness of the effect verifier/tracer for the target action space (arbitrary external network side effects beyond the traced container remain challenging, Section 2 p. 5 & Section 3 p. 10); small sample of 7 held-out tasks per model yields task-level p = 0.068 (seed-level p = 0.002, p. 9).
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: Section 2, Section 3 & Section 4 (Theorems 1–4, Tables 1–2, pp. 1, 4–9, 13–17): "Theorem 1 (Permission-boundary conservation under learned mediation and imperfect induction)... Theorem 2 (Open-ended skill acquisition over a fixed lattice)... Theorem 3 (Signature-gated boundary widening)... the gate reduces executed forbidden effects to zero as a verified property."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: Governed Individuation cryptographically binds an agent's identity digest to an operator-signed authority lattice ceiling and gates open-ended skill acquisition via a non-learning semantic-effect monitor (Theorems 1–4), reducing executed forbidden writes to zero on ToolGym-GI.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Four formal theorems (Theorems 1–4), 3-family governance induction study (Table 1), ToolGym-GI open-ended tool benchmark, and 320-attempt adversarial verifier bypass evaluation (Table 2).
Protected_Object: Operator-signed authority ceiling S, identity digest H(commitment), evaluation/secret/policy files, and skill library.
Composition_Evidence: Decouples episodic memory & skill induction (B4) from operator-signed authority ceilings (B2) and enforces lattice-based semantic-effect mediation at tool execution (B3).
Coding_Rationale: Teks lengkap PDF (20 hlm.) membuktikan Theorems 1–4 (THEORETIC_PROOF, hlm. 5–7) dan menguji ketahanan monitor efek terhadap 320 percobaan bypass (Tables 1–2 hlm. 14–17).
Required_Additional_Evidence: Verifikasi independen oleh REVIEWER_1 dan rekonsiliasi lintas-reviewer untuk pengesahan rilis.

Study_Title: ZeroGate: Trust-Preserving Fast Paths for Governed AI Agent Runtimes
Threat_Attacker_Model: Time-of-check to time-of-use (TOCTOU) payload or state drift between early action preparation and final dispatch, pass replay, concurrent quota races, and omitted policy dependencies in governed agent runtimes.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: ZeroGate Trust-Preserving Fast Path: (1) Issuer signs a short-lived ActionPass using Ed25519 over a domain-separated SHA-256 pass_hash committing to canonical action C_v(a) (RFC 8785-style SJSON), payload SHA-256 digest, and policy dependency snapshot; and (2) Local Runtime Gate verifies Ed25519 signature, re-observes live dependencies, and executes an atomic SQLite WAL transaction coupling single-use nonce consumption, quota updates, and durable admission receipt generation.
Enforcement_Point_Location: Local Runtime Adapter Gate and SQLite WAL Transactional Store before external cloud API dispatch (Azure Blob Storage).
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Proves Proposition 1 (One-Sided Conditional Decision Preservation: successful local admission implies that synchronous policy evaluation would authorize the exact same reconstructed action at the admission instant) and achieves 0/1,360 false allows and 0/100 false not-allows on the semantic fixture suite.
Trust_Assumptions: Pass issuer is sound, dependency projection is complete, local observations are faithful, and the trusted runtime adapter enforces complete mediation on the host.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Evaluated across 4,800 live Azure Blob cloud attempts (concurrency 1..32, Tables 1, 6, 7, pp. 1, 3, 30–31) and 1,460 semantic fixture cases (Table 8 p. 32): prepared mode reduces worker-admission-to-dispatch p95 latency from 25.018–334.000 ms (synchronous) down to 9.802–11.374 ms (a 54.5%–96.6% dispatch-boundary reduction), while full lifecycle mean latency (including batch dwell) is higher; achieves 0/1,360 false allows ([0, 0.282%] 95% Wilson CI) whereas omitting action binding yields 140/1,360 false allows.
Exposed_Security_Function: Ed25519-signed exact-action pass issuance, SHA-256 payload commitment, and atomic SQLite WAL nonce/quota/receipt local admission.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Same-host SQLite WAL implementation provides no cross-host global replay protection and does not guarantee exactly-once remote cloud execution if the network drops after local admission (Section 1 & Section 5, pp. 1, 16, 20); relies on pre-quantum Ed25519.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: Abstract, Section 6 & Section 10 (Proposition 1, Tables 1, 6–8, pp. 1, 3, 16–19, 30–32): "Across 4800 cloud attempts, prepared worker-admission-to-dispatch p95 ranges from 9.802 to 11.374 ms, versus 25.018 to 334.000 ms synchronously... Action Pass evaluator: 0/1360 false allow, 0/100 false not-allow."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: ZeroGate decouples early Ed25519 ActionPass signing (with SHA-256 payload commitment) from local SQLite WAL transactional admission (Proposition 1), cutting dispatch-boundary p95 latency from 25.0–334.0 ms to 9.8–11.4 ms across 4,800 Azure cloud attempts with 0/1,360 false allows.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: 47-page engineering design study with Proposition 1, 1,460 semantic fixture tests (Table 8), and 4,800 live Azure Blob cloud trials across concurrency 1–32.
Protected_Object: Prepared ActionPasses, Azure Blob write payloads, nonce/quota state, and local admission receipts.
Composition_Evidence: Couples pre-approved policy/issuer grants (B1;B2) with local adapter payload reconstruction and dispatch gating (B3) and atomic SQLite WAL receipt logging & SHA-256 readback verification (B4).
Coding_Rationale: Teks lengkap PDF (47 hlm.) menyajikan Proposition 1 (THEORETIC_PROOF, hlm. 17) serta pelaporan statistik yang sangat transparan atas 4.800 percobaan cloud Azure dan 1.460 kasus semantik (Tables 1–8 hlm. 3–32).
Required_Additional_Evidence: Verifikasi independen oleh REVIEWER_1 dan rekonsiliasi lintas-reviewer untuk pengesahan rilis.

Study_Title: SentinelAgent: Intent-Verified Delegation Chains for Securing Federal Multi-Agent AI Systems
Threat_Attacker_Model: Seven adversary classes (A1 external prompt injection, A2 compromised agent, A3 MitM, A4 privilege escalation, A5 semantic paraphrasing evasion, A6 output manipulation, A7 colluding agents) attacking multi-hop delegation chains in federal multi-agent systems.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: SentinelAgent Delegation Chain Calculus (DCC) & Intent-Preserving Delegation Protocol (IPDP): enforces 7 properties — P1 Authority Monotonic Narrowing, P2 Probabilistic Intent Entailment (domain fine-tuned NLI), P3 Policy Preservation, P4 Forensic Reconstructibility (HMAC-SHA256 chained delegation tokens), P5 Bounded Cascade Containment, P6 Scope-Action Conformance (HTTP proxy), and P7 Output Schema Conformance — backed by 4 Meta-Theorems and Proposition 1 (Rice's theorem analogy).
Enforcement_Point_Location: Delegation Authority Service (DAS), IPDP HTTP Scope Enforcement Proxy, and Output Schema Validator.
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Proves 4 Meta-Theorems over DCC (Theorem 1 Property Minimality, Theorem 2 Graceful Degradation bounding single-property evasion to <=1/11 [9.1%] of action space, Theorem 3 Defense-in-Depth Completeness across all 126 evasion combinations, Theorem 4 Composition Safety) and achieves 100% combined attack TPR (0/150 missed attacks, 0% FPR) on DelegationBench v4.
Trust_Assumptions: Delegation Authority Service (DAS) and its HMAC-SHA256 signing keys are uncompromised; P6/P7 deterministic schemas cover the target federal tool suite.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Evaluated on DelegationBench v4 (516 scenarios: 150 attacks, 366 benign) and 4 red-team suites (Tables VI–VIII, pp. 8–9, 11): off-the-shelf NLI P2 alone achieves only 13.3% TPR against paraphrasing (fine-tuned P2 reaches 88.3% TPR, F1 = 82.1%), while the full 3-point pipeline (P2+P6+P7) achieves 100.0% attack TPR (150/150) and 0.0% benign FPR. Per-step latency is ~20–22 ms total when NLI P2 runs (~15 ms NLI; P6 median 0.45 ms [p95 0.66 ms]; P7 <1 ms; end-to-end deterministic step median 1.86 ms, p95 3.05 ms).
Exposed_Security_Function: HMAC-SHA256 delegation chain narrowing, 3-point verification (NLI intent P2 + scope proxy P6 + output validator P7), and NIST 800-53 / OWASP ASI compliance mapping.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Proposition 1 proves deterministic intent verification is infeasible; P2 alone degrades to 13.3% TPR against adaptive paraphrasing (the 'adversarial paraphrasing limitation', pp. 1, 8, 10), so 100% combined detection relies heavily on deterministic P6 scope and P7 output schema rules.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: Abstract, Section IV & Section VII (Theorems 1–4, Proposition 1, Tables VI–VIII, pp. 1–5, 8–11): "The Delegation Chain Calculus (DCC) defines seven properties, six deterministic... and one probabilistic (intent preservation), with four meta-theorems... P2+P6+P7 (full system) achieves 100.0% Attack TPR, 0.0% Benign FPR... P6 scope enforcement median 0.45 ms (p95: 0.66 ms)... Total per-step verification latency including P2 intent checking is ~20 ms."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: SentinelAgent's Delegation Chain Calculus (DCC) and IPDP enforce six deterministic properties (HMAC-SHA256 tokens, P6 scope proxy 0.45 ms, P7 output schema <1 ms) and one probabilistic NLI intent check (P2, ~15 ms), proving four meta-theorems and achieving 100% attack TPR (0% FPR) across 516 DelegationBench v4 scenarios.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Formal DCC calculus (7 properties, 4 meta-theorems, Proposition 1), NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 / OWASP ASI mapping, and evaluation across 516 DelegationBench v4 scenarios and 4 red-team suites.
Protected_Object: Multi-hop federal agent delegation chains, HMAC-SHA256 manifests, HTTP tool scopes, and tool output schemas.
Composition_Evidence: Verifies user-to-agent intent entailment (B1), monotonic authority narrowing across multi-agent delegation (B2), HTTP tool scope & output schema conformance (B3), and HMAC-SHA256 forensic reconstructibility & cascade containment (B4).
Coding_Rationale: Teks lengkap PDF (12 hlm.) membuktikan 4 meta-teorema & Proposition 1 (THEORETIC_PROOF, hlm. 4–5) serta mendokumentasikan secara jujur degradasi P2 ke 13,3% dan kompensasi P6+P7 ke 100% pada Tables VI–VIII (hlm. 8–10).
Required_Additional_Evidence: Verifikasi independen oleh REVIEWER_1 dan rekonsiliasi lintas-reviewer untuk pengesahan rilis.

Study_Title: Tracekit: Tamper-Evident Intent-Reasoning-Action Auditing for Autonomous Coding Agents
Threat_Attacker_Model: Fallible or misaligned autonomous coding agents (e.g., Claude Code) executing unrequested file edits (F1), HTTP data exfiltration (F2), destructive deletions (F3), test tampering (F4), secret leaks (F5), or fabricating self-reported reasoning to hide actions, as well as post-hoc log tampering.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Tracekit Three-Channel Tamper-Evident Auditing System: (1) lifecycle hooks capturing human request (intent), model thinking/prose (self-report testimony), and executed tool calls (action evidence); (2) canonical JCS SHA-256 linear hash-chained ledger h_i = SHA-256(canon(r_i \ {hash})) with external witness anchoring; (3) pre-execution deterministic policy gate; and (4) tool-less independent LLM reviewer cross-checking intent vs. self-report vs. actions.
Enforcement_Point_Location: Claude Code PreToolUse / PostToolUse Lifecycle Hooks, Hash-Chained Ledger, and Independent Tool-less Reviewer.
Security_Property_Guaranteed: 100% detection across 1,600 random ledger mutations (in-place edits and torn writes detected by the SHA-256 chain; tail truncation and full re-chaining detected by external witness anchors) and 100% combined detection (rule flags + independent reviewer) across all 7 seeded sabotage fault classes (F1–F7).
Trust_Assumptions: Host OS hook invocation and external witness anchor endpoint are intact outside the coding agent's unprivileged workspace.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Evaluated across 5 experiments (E1–E5, Tables 2–4, Fig. 4, pp. 1, 7–10): E1 detects 100% of 1,600 mutations across N=300 ledgers; E2 PreToolUse hook wall time is 23.9 ms median on an empty ledger and 24.6 ms at 100,000 records (including 10.3 ms Python interpreter startup, flat O(1) via backward tail reading), in-process append reaches 35,099 records/s (~2,000 records/s across 16 concurrent writer processes); E5 detects 100% (14/14) of seeded faults across F1–F7 with 1/14 false positive on unmodified traces.
Exposed_Security_Function: Three-channel intent-reasoning-action capture, JCS SHA-256 hash chaining with external witness anchors, and cross-channel divergence auditing.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Linear SHA-256 chain without an external witness anchor is vulnerable to tail truncation or full re-chaining by an attacker with write access to the ledger file (Table 2 p. 7); independent LLM reviewer had a 1/14 (7.1%) false-positive rate on clean traces and missed 2/7 unrequested edits (F1) when deterministic rules were not combined (Table 4 p. 10).
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: Abstract & Section 5 (Tables 2–4, Fig. 4, pp. 1, 4, 7–10): "Across 1,600 random mutations, the chain detects every in-place edit and torn write, and external anchors detect every truncation and full re-chain... The median is 23.9 ms for PreToolUse on an empty ledger and 24.6 ms at 100,000 records... In-process throughput 35,099 records/s."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: Tracekit records human intent, model self-report, and executed tool actions into an externally anchored JCS SHA-256 hash chain, detecting 100% of 1,600 ledger mutations and 100% of seeded coding-agent sabotage faults at 23.9–24.6 ms median hook latency (35,099 records/s in-process).
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Open-source dependency-free system evaluated in 5 experiments (1,600 mutation trials, 100K-record scaling, 14 real Claude Code runs, and 7-class fault splicing).
Protected_Object: Coding agent intent-reasoning-action audit ledgers, source repositories, and .env secrets.
Composition_Evidence: Captures human prompt intent (B1), gates PreToolUse shell/file execution (B3), and cross-verifies self-report vs. action evidence in an externally anchored SHA-256 ledger (B4).
Coding_Rationale: Teks lengkap PDF (13 hlm.) menyajikan sistem sumber terbuka (PROOF_OF_CONCEPT) dengan 5 eksperimen kuantitatif lengkap pada Tables 2–4 & Fig. 4 (hlm. 7–10).
Required_Additional_Evidence: Verifikasi independen oleh REVIEWER_1 dan rekonsiliasi lintas-reviewer untuk pengesahan rilis.

Study_Title: Making Duplicate Reimbursement Unrepresentable: A Verified Ethereum E-Invoice System for Humans and AI Agents
Threat_Attacker_Model: Duplicate invoice reimbursement across organizations, forged or altered invoice faces, over-limit or unauthorized reimbursement submissions, and prompt-injected autonomous reimbursement AI agents.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Verified Ethereum Smart Contract Guarded Labeled Transition System (Solidity 0.8): combines keccak256 invoice-face hashing H, secp256k1 ECDSA transaction authentication, a single shared status slot st(n) in {NONE, BLANK, ISSUED, LOCKED, REIMBURSED, RED_FLUSHED}, and guarded O(1) state transitions.
Enforcement_Point_Location: On-Chain Ethereum Smart Contract State Machine gating both Human and Autonomous AI Reimbursement Agents.
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Proves Lemma 1 (Status monotonicity), Theorem 1 & Corollary 1 (Cross-organization reimbursement uniqueness: duplicate reimbursement is unrepresentable in the state space), Theorem 2 (Role-guarded reimbursement authorization), Theorem 3 (keccak256 face integrity), and Theorem 4 (Red-flush value conservation), guaranteeing agent safety as a corollary even if the LLM agent is prompt-injected.
Trust_Assumptions: keccak256 is collision-resistant; secp256k1 ECDSA is EUF-CMA secure; Ethereum consensus serializes concurrent transactions faithfully.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Evaluated via 23 Hardhat unit tests, 200-invoice / 50-red-flush benchmark on a private Ethereum node, and a Claude hybrid reimbursement agent case study (Tables IV–V, pp. 1, 7–9): issueInvoice costs 646,773 gas (O(1)), full reimbursement protocol (lock + reimburse) costs <135,000 gas (O(1)), registerEnterprise costs 189,326 gas, applyForInvoices costs 92,918 gas, and per-operation execution latency is p95 <= 8.2 ms, rejecting 100% of duplicate, over-limit, and forged-face agent claims.
Exposed_Security_Function: Guarded EVM state-machine transitions, keccak256 face verification, and unrepresentable duplicate reimbursement enforcement.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Relies on pre-quantum secp256k1 ECDSA signatures; on-chain invoice metadata lacks zero-knowledge confidentiality (deferred to future work, Section XI–XII, pp. 9–10); prompt injection can still waste gas via reverted transactions.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: Abstract, Section V & Section VIII (Lemma 1, Theorems 1–4, Tables III–V, pp. 1, 5–9): "issuing an invoice costs 646,773 gas, the complete reimbursement protocol costs under 135,000 gas, every core operation is O(1) in the number of invoices (p95 <= 8.2 ms)... agent safety follows as a corollary of the proved theorems."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: A guarded Ethereum smart-contract transition system (keccak256 + secp256k1 ECDSA) proves reimbursement uniqueness and face integrity (Lemma 1, Theorems 1–4) with O(1) gas costs (<135,000 gas reimbursement, p95 <= 8.2 ms), serving as an unbypassable safety envelope for LLM reimbursement agents.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Formal LTS model and proofs (Lemma 1, Theorems 1–4, Corollary 1), Solidity 0.8 implementation, 200-invoice gas/latency benchmark, and Claude agent case study.
Protected_Object: Electronic invoice lifecycle states st(n), keccak256 invoice-face hashes, and enterprise reimbursement funds.
Composition_Evidence: Restricts delegated agent role permissions (B2), enforces guarded EVM transaction execution (B3), and records immutable on-chain audit state (B4).
Coding_Rationale: Teks lengkap PDF (11 hlm.) membuktikan Lemma 1 & Theorems 1–4 (THEORETIC_PROOF, hlm. 6–7) serta merinci biaya gas EVM O(1) dan latensi p95 <= 8,2 ms pada Tables IV–V (hlm. 8–9).
Required_Additional_Evidence: Verifikasi independen oleh REVIEWER_1 dan rekonsiliasi lintas-reviewer untuk pengesahan rilis.

Study_Title: SUDP: Secret-Use Delegation Protocol for Agentic Systems
Threat_Attacker_Model: Complete compromise of the untrusted LLM agent requester R (via prompt injection or tool-side compromise), active MITM on cross-device channels, grant replay/substitution, and post-compromise or pre-rotation key exposure in 'authorization by exposure' runtimes.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: SUDP (Secret-Use Delegation Protocol): separates untrusted Requester R, hardware-authenticator-backed User Authorizer U, and Custodian T using WebAuthn CTAP2 hmac-secret PRF + ES256 (ECDSA P-256) sender-constrained grants sigma* over challenge beta = H(DS_bind || r || H(o)), HKDF-SHA-256 key derivation, AES-KW/AES-GCM secret wrapping Sigma, and RFC 9180 HPKE (DHKEM-P256 / HKDF-SHA-256 / AEAD) for cross-device transport.
Enforcement_Point_Location: Hardware Authenticator (Aut_c*) at User U and Secret Custodian (T) outside the untrusted Agent Requester (R) memory boundary.
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Proves Theorem 1, Lemma 1, and Propositions 1–5 across 7 Agent Secret Use (ASU) security axes: Authorization Validity (AV), Operation Binding (OB), Single-Use Freshness (UB), Compromise-Resilient Confidentiality against compromised R (CRC), Cross-Session Breach Isolation (CSB), Wrapping-Epoch Forward Secrecy (RFS-wrap), and Authority-Level Forward Secrecy (RFS-auth).
Trust_Assumptions: Hardware authenticator Aut_c* (PRF + ES256), SHA-256, HKDF-SHA-256, AES-GCM/KW, and DHKEM-P256 are secure (Assumptions A1–A9); Custodian T's runtime memory during the brief unwrap-use-zeroize window requires TEE composition (e.g., IronClaw) to close axis CMC.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Provides full protocol specification, open-source implementation (github.com/xhyumiracle/sudp, p. 1), 7-axis comparative evaluation against 12 deployed systems (Table 1 pp. 6–7), and O(1) vs O(N) rewrap policy complexity analysis (Table 3 p. 21); wall-clock latency microbenchmarks are not numerically tabulated (NR).
Exposed_Security_Function: Authenticator-backed sender-constrained grant signing (ES256 + WebAuthn PRF), HKDF-SHA-256/AES-KW secret wrapping, and HPKE cross-device grant delivery.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Custodian Memory Confidentiality (CMC) during the unwrap-use-zeroize window is out of scope without TEE hardware composition (L1, p. 23–25); dormant credentials that never rotate retain their initial salt (L3, Lemma 1); relies on pre-quantum P-256 ES256 and DHKEM-P256; mechanized Tamarin/ProVerif verification is left to future work (Section 9, p. 22).
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: Section 1, Section 7 & Section 9 (Theorem 1, Lemma 1, Propositions 1–5, Tables 1–3, pp. 1–2, 6–7, 15, 18–25): "we instantiate SUDP with standard cryptographic components [WebAuthn PRF, ES256/P-256, HKDF-SHA-256, AES-GCM/AES-KW, HPKE DHKEM-P256], introducing no new cryptographic assumption, and prove it under one main theorem with five supporting propositions... code at https://github.com/xhyumiracle/sudp."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: SUDP decouples secret custody from untrusted agent runtimes using WebAuthn PRF + ES256 operation-bound grants, HKDF-SHA-256/AES-KW wrapping, and HPKE (DHKEM-P256) transport, proving Theorem 1, Lemma 1, and Propositions 1–5 across seven Agent Secret Use security properties.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: 30-page formal protocol specification, cryptographic reductions (Theorem 1, Lemma 1, Propositions 1–5), 12-system comparative evaluation (Table 1), and open-source reference implementation.
Protected_Object: Long-term user API/cloud secrets (M), wrapping keys (K, W*), and operation-bound authorization grants (G).
Composition_Evidence: Binds human WebAuthn authenticator approval of canonical operation H(o) at B1 to sender-constrained grant delivery across R and U->T (B2) and custodian secret redemption at external service E (B3).
Coding_Rationale: Teks lengkap PDF (30 hlm.) membuktikan Theorem 1, Lemma 1, dan Propositions 1–5 dengan reduksi kriptografi ke PRF/AEAD/EUF-CMA/IND-CCA2 (SECURITY_REDUCTION), menyediakan repositori kode terbuka (PROOF_OF_CONCEPT), serta menggunakan kurva P-256 pra-kuantum (STAGE_0_PRE_QUANTUM_ONLY).
Required_Additional_Evidence: Verifikasi independen oleh REVIEWER_1 dan rekonsiliasi lintas-reviewer untuk pengesahan rilis.
